Mom and Dad kissed them and said, "We love you, too, Tom and Lily. But you have to learn from your mistake. You have to be careful and responsible. You have to respect the things you have and the things you use. You have to think before you act. And you have to say sorry when you do something wrong."

Tom and Lily nodded and said, "We understand, Mom and Dad. We will try to be better. We will try to make you happy. We will try to make good marks, not bad marks."

"Look, Ben, I can make shapes with my mouth in the mist!" Sam says. He blows out air and makes a circle.

"Wow, that is cool, Sam! Can you teach me how to do that?" Ben asks.

"Sure, Ben, it is easy. You just make a small hole with your lips and blow out hard. Like this." Sam shows Ben how to make a circle.

Ben tries to do the same. He makes a small hole with his lips and blows out hard. But he does not make a circle. He makes a big noise. "Pfffft!"

Sam laughs. "Ben, that is not a circle, that is a fart!"

Ben feels sad. He thinks Sam is making fun of him. He does not want to play with Sam anymore. He runs away.

Sam sees Ben run away. He feels sorry. He did not mean to hurt Ben's feelings. He runs after Ben.

"Ben, wait, I am sorry. I was not making fun of you. I was just joking. You are my friend. I want to play with you." Sam says.

Ben stops and looks at Sam. He sees Sam's face. Sam looks sad too. Ben thinks Sam is sorry. He does not want to be mad at Sam. He wants to play with Sam too.

"Of course, Ben, I will teach you. Come on, let's try again. And then we can make other shapes too. Like a heart, or a star, or a smiley face." Sam says.

Ben and Sam hug. They go back to the mist. They blow out air and make shapes. They have fun.

The moral of the story is: Friends should not make fun of each other. Friends should help each other and say sorry when they make a mistake. Friends should have fun together.

The gorilla saw them, and he did not like them. He did not want them to cross the line, and touch the rope. He wanted them to stay away from his cage, and his home. He was angry, and he was not patient.

He roared at them, and he banged on the cage. He showed them his big teeth, and his sharp claws. He scared them, and he made them cry.

"His name is Spot," Anna said. "He is my best friend. Can I have a real puppy for my birthday, mom?"

"But I'm curious!" Lily said. "I want to have an adventure!"

"You can have an adventure somewhere else. Like in the backyard or in the playroom. But not in the basement. Come on, let's go upstairs. I'll show you my new puzzle. It has a lot of pieces and colors. It's fun and challenging." Max said.

Lily thought for a moment. She still wanted to see the door, but she also liked puzzles. And she did not want to get in trouble with Mom and Dad. Maybe she could come back another day when they were not home. She nodded and followed Max upstairs. She decided to be adventurous in a safer way.

"Wow, it can spray water too!" he exclaimed.

He picked up the iron and aimed it at Sara. He pressed the button again and again, making the water come out faster.

"Stop it, Tom, you're wetting me!" Sara cried, trying to dodge the water.

But Tom didn't stop. He thought it was funny. He ran after Sara with the iron, still spraying water.

Sara ran to the stairs, but she slipped on the wet floor. She fell down and hit her head on the edge of a step. She lay still and didn't make a sound.

Tom stopped and looked at Sara. He saw blood on her head and on the floor. He dropped the iron and started to cry.

The boy laughed and threw another stick. The dog chased it again. The woman ran after the dog and tried to catch him. The boy thought it was funny and threw more sticks.

"Ha ha! You can't catch me! You are slow!" he said.

But then, a big man came to the park. He was the boy's father. He saw what the boy was doing and was very cross. He walked to the boy and grabbed his arm.

"What are you doing? You are naughty! You hurt the woman and her dog!" he said.

The boy was scared and stopped laughing. He looked at the woman and her dog and felt sorry. He said to them:

"I'm sorry. I was naughty. I won't do it again."

The woman and her dog came back. The woman was still angry, but she saw that the boy was sorry. She said to him:

"Thank you for saying sorry. Don't be naughty again. Be kind to animals and people."

The boy nodded and said:

"I will. I'm sorry."

The woman and her dog left the park. The big man took the boy home. He said to him:

"You are naughty. You need to learn. You will have no toys and no TV today."

The boy was sad and said:

"I'm sorry. I will learn. I will be good."

Buddy's owner, a little girl named Amy, saw Buddy and the hanger stuck in the freeze. She ran to help them. Amy pulled Buddy and the hanger out of the freeze. Buddy was so happy that he wagged his tail and licked Amy's face. Buddy and the hanger were safe, and they all went inside to get warm.

"Mom, can I play with the other kids?" Tim asked. "Of course, Tim! Just be nice and share," his mom said. So, Tim went to play with the other kids. They were all building a big sandcastle together. But Tim felt tired and wanted to quit.

"Guys, I want to quit," Tim said. The other kids looked at him and said, "No, Tim! Don't quit! We can all finish the sandcastle together!" So, Tim decided not to quit and kept on playing with the other kids. They all worked together, and soon they made a huge, beautiful sandcastle.

In the end, Tim was happy that he didn't quit. He learned that when you work together with friends, you can do great things. And that day at the beach, Tim made new friends and had lots of fun.

The little girl went home and saved her money. She was very patient. After some days, she had enough money. She went back to the shop and bought the pretty image for her mom. Her mom was very happy, and they both thanked the man who sold the image.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a journal. He liked to draw in his journal every day. He drew pictures of his family, his friends, and his toys. Tim's journal was very special to him.

One hot day, Tim went to the park with his mom. He brought his journal with him so he could draw the trees and the birds. But when it was time to go home, Tim forgot his journal at the park. He was very sad.

The next day, Tim and his mom went back to the park to find the journal. They looked everywhere. Finally, Tim saw his journal under a big tree. He recognized it because of the stickers on the cover. Tim was so happy to have his journal back. From that day on, he always remembered to keep his journal safe.

One day, a little dog named Max went for a walk. Max was an obedient dog, and he always listened to his mom. As Max walked, he found a scarf. It was a pretty scarf, and Max wanted to show it to his mom.

Max picked up the scarf with his mouth and ran home. When he got home, his mom said, "Max, you are dirty! You need to bathe before you come inside." Max did not want to bathe, but he was an obedient dog, so he listened to his mom.

Max took a bath and got all clean. Then, he showed his mom the pretty scarf. His mom said, "Good job, Max! You are a very obedient dog. I am proud of you." Max was happy, and he wagged his tail.

The cake was so big that it needed a special place to hang. The people at the party found a big tree to hang the cake. They put the cake in the tree so everyone could see it. The cake looked so pretty hanging in the tree.

When it was time to eat the cake, everyone gathered around the tree. They took the cake down and put it on a big table. Everyone got a piece of the cake. It was the best cake they ever had. The party was so much fun, and everyone was happy.

One day, a big whale named Willy set out on a perfect sunny day to find a new friend. He swam in the big blue sea, splashing his tail and making big waves. Willy was very happy and excited to find a new friend to play with.

As Willy swam, he saw a little fish named Finny. Willy said, "Hi, Finny! Will you be my friend?" Finny looked at the big whale and smiled. "Yes, Willy! I would love to be your friend!" Finny said with a big grin.

Willy and Finny played all day in the perfect blue sea. They swam fast and slow, and they jumped high in the air. They laughed and had so much fun. At the end of the day, the sun set, and the two friends said goodbye. Willy and Finny knew they would have many more perfect days together as best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia liked to sort her toys into different groups. She sorted them by color, by size, and by type. One day, she found an interesting toy. It was a round ball that looked like a planet.

Mia showed the planet toy to her friend, Tom. "Look, Tom! I found an interesting planet toy!" she said. Tom looked at the planet and said, "Wow! That is a very interesting toy. Can I play with it?" Mia said, "Yes, but be careful. It's my favorite toy now."

Tom and Mia played with the planet toy all day. They pretended it was a real planet and they were astronauts exploring space. But then, Tom accidentally threw the planet toy too hard. It hit a big rock and broke into pieces.

Mia was very sad. She said, "Tom, you broke my interesting planet toy! I told you to be careful." Tom felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, Mia. I didn't mean to break it." But the planet toy was broken, and Mia was sad for the rest of the day.

The bird felt the love from Max and started to feel better. Soon, the bird could fly again. Max and the bird became best friends. They played together and were happy every day.

One day, the people in the town decided to punish the noisy person. They took away his loud music and told him to be quiet. The noisy person was very sad and promised to be quiet from now on.

But the noisy person did not keep his promise. He started to shout and play loud music again. The people in the town were very angry. They punished the noisy person again, but this time they sent him far away from the town. The noisy person was all alone and sad, with no one to talk to or play with.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to paint. She would paint all day long. She painted the sun, the moon, the trees, and the flowers. Her mom and dad would watch her and smile.

One day, Lily was feeling restless. She couldn't think of anything new to paint. So, her mom said, "Lily, why don't you paint a memory? Think of a happy time we had together and paint that." Lily thought for a moment and remembered a day at the park with her mom and dad.

Lily started to paint. She painted herself, her mom, and her dad at the park. They were playing with a big, red ball. When she finished, she showed her painting to her mom and dad. They smiled and said, "Lily, this is a beautiful memory. We should always remember the happy times we share together."

The moral of the story is to cherish the happy memories with our loved ones.

Spot's mom saw him and said, "Oh no! Let me give your leg a massage to make it feel better." She gently rubbed his leg, and it started to feel better. Spot was happy and wagged his tail.

The next day, Spot saw a dead tree in the park. He barked at it and said, "You can't hurt me, tree! I am strong and fast!" Spot ran around the tree, showing off his speed. His friends cheered, and they all played together again.

Mia and Leo went to the zoo with their mom. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and giraffes. They liked to watch them and learn their names.

Then they came to the ostrich pen. The ostrich was very big and had long legs and a long neck. It had black and white feathers and a small head. Mia and Leo wanted to feed it some grass, but the ostrich refused.

"No, no, no!" the ostrich said. "I don't want grass. I want something else."

Mia and Leo were confused. What did the ostrich want? They looked around and saw some popcorn, some carrots, and some apples. They tried to give them to the ostrich, but the ostrich refused again.

"No, no, no!" the ostrich said. "I don't want popcorn, carrots, or apples. I want something else."

Mia and Leo were frustrated. They didn't know what the ostrich wanted. They asked their mom for help, but she didn't know either. She said the ostrich was very picky and stubborn.

Then they saw a boy with a red balloon. The boy was happy and played with his balloon. The ostrich saw the balloon too and wanted it. It stretched its neck and tried to grab the balloon with its beak.

"Hey, that's mine!" the boy said. "Give it back!"

But the ostrich didn't listen. It ran away with the balloon and tried to fit it in its pen. But the balloon was too big and popped. The ostrich was sad and cried.

Mia and Leo felt sorry for the ostrich. They decided to give it a hug and say sorry. The ostrich felt better and said thank you. It learned to share and be nice. Mia and Leo learned to be patient and kind. They all became friends and had fun at the zoo.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a big box. They want to make a house with the box.

They use a marker to draw a door and windows on the box. They cut out the door and windows with scissors. They find some flowers and leaves to decorate the box. They are happy with their house.

They invite their other friends to see their house. Their friends like it too. They take turns to go inside and pretend to cook and sleep and read. Tom and Jen provide snacks and drinks for their friends. They share and have fun.

Tom and Jen are proud of their house. They think it is the best house in the park. They hug each other and smile. They have success. They have a clear idea of what they want to do next. They want to make a car with another box.

Lily loved to play the flute. She had a shiny flute that made pretty sounds when she blew into it. She learned how to play from her big sister, who was very good at music. Lily wanted to be like her sister, but she was humble. She knew she had to practice a lot and listen to her teacher.

One day, Lily had a flute lesson at school. She was excited to show her teacher what she had learned. She put her flute in her backpack and got ready to go. But when she got to school, she could not find her flute. She looked everywhere, but it was gone. She felt very sad and scared. Who took her flute? How could she play without it?

She ran to her teacher and told her what happened. Her teacher was kind and gentle. She said, "Don't worry, Lily. We will find your flute. Maybe someone borrowed it by mistake. Or maybe you left it somewhere else. Let's ask your friends and look around the school. I promise we will find it."

Lily felt a little better. She trusted her teacher. She asked her friends if they had seen her flute. Some of them said no, and some of them said maybe. They helped her look in the classroom, the playground, the library, and the cafeteria. But they could not find it.

Lily was about to give up. She thought she would never see her flute again. She felt like crying. But then, she heard a familiar sound. It was her flute! She followed the sound and found a boy playing it in the music room. He was not very good at it. He made loud and funny noises. Lily was angry and happy at the same time. She said, "Hey, that's my flute! Give it back to me!"

The boy looked surprised and scared. He said, "I'm sorry, I didn't know it was yours. I found it in the hall. I wanted to try it. I like the flute. It's cool."

Lily said, "It's not cool to take things that are not yours. You should ask first. The flute is very special to me. I love it. Please give it back."

The boy said, "OK, OK, I'm sorry. Here, take it. I won't do it again. I promise."

Lily took her flute and checked it. It was still shiny and pretty. She was glad it was not broken or lost. She said, "Thank you for giving it back. And thank you for promising. Promises are important. You should keep them."

The boy said, "You're welcome. And you're right. Promises are important. I will keep them. Can we be friends?"

Lily smiled and nodded. She said, "Yes, we can be friends. But only if you promise to be nice and honest. And maybe, if you want, I can teach you how to play the flute better. It's fun and easy. You just have to practice and listen."

The boy smiled and nodded. He said, "Yes, I promise. And yes, I want. You are very kind and humble. And you are very good at the flute. You can teach me. I will practice and listen."

Lily and the boy hugged and became friends. They played the flute together and had fun. They kept their promises and learned from each other. They were happy.

Tim and Lily were gifted children. They liked to learn new things and play with puzzles and books. One day, they found a big bottle of bubble soap in the garden. They wanted to make bubbles and have fun.

They took the bottle and a wand and went to the porch. They dipped the wand in the soap and blew gently. Many bubbles came out and floated in the air. They were shiny and colorful. Tim and Lily laughed and clapped. They tried to catch the bubbles and pop them.

"Look, Lily, I can make a big bubble!" Tim said. He blew harder and made a huge bubble. It was bigger than his head. He was very proud.

"Wow, Tim, that's amazing!" Lily said. She wanted to make a big bubble too. She blew harder and harder, but her bubbles were small and weak. She felt sad and angry.

"Tim, can I use your wand?" she asked. "Maybe mine is broken."

"Sorry, Lily, this is my wand. I found it first. You can use your own wand." Tim said. He did not want to share. He liked his wand and his big bubbles.

Lily felt more sad and angry. She wanted to have fun too. She had an idea. She waited until Tim was busy making another big bubble. Then she ran to him and removed his wand from his hand. She ran away with it.

"Hey, Lily, give it back!" Tim shouted. He was very mad. He chased Lily around the porch. But Lily was faster. She ran and ran, holding the wand.

As they ran, they did not see the steps. They tripped and fell. The wand broke in two. The bottle of soap spilled on the ground. There were no more bubbles. Tim and Lily cried.

Mom heard the noise and came to see. She saw the broken wand, the spilled soap, and the crying children. She was not happy.

"What happened here?" she asked.

"Tim and Lily told her what they did. They blamed each other. They said sorry.

Mom shook her head. She said, "Tim and Lily, you are gifted children, but you are not kind children. You need to learn to share and be nice. Bubbles are fun, but friends are more important. If you want to have fun, you need to have fun together. Do you understand?"

Tim and Lily nodded. They felt sorry. They hugged each other. They said sorry again.

Mom smiled. She said, "It's okay. I love you both. I have another bottle of soap in the house. Do you want to try again?"

Tim and Lily nodded. They said yes. They thanked Mom. They took the new bottle and a new wand. They went to the porch. They dipped the wand in the soap and blew gently. Many bubbles came out and floated in the air. They were shiny and colorful. Tim and Lily laughed and clapped. They tried to catch the bubbles and pop them. They shared the wand and the soap. They had fun together. They were happy.

They hop on the hill and get closer to the hole. They see smoke and fire coming out of the hole. They are scared and surprised. They hear a loud noise like a roar.

"Run, Mia, run!" Tim shouts. "The volcano is angry!"

They hop down the hill as fast as they can. They see rocks and ash flying in the air. They run to their house and hide under the table.

They are safe, but they are sorry. They did not know the hill was a real volcano. They did not mean to make the volcano angry.

They hug each other and say, "I'm sorry, Tim. I'm sorry, Mia. We are still friends."

They hope the volcano will calm down soon. They hope they can play outside again. They hope they can find a new place to play that is not a volcano.

Tim and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big pool. It has blue water and a slide. Tim and Mia want to swim in the pool.

"Can we go in the pool, please?" Tim asks his mom.

"Sorry, no. The pool is not for us. It is for big kids only. You are too small." Tim's mom says.

Tim is sad. He stares at the pool. He sees the big kids splash and laugh. He wants to have fun too.

Mia is not sad. She has an idea. She sees a hose near the pool. She runs to the hose and turns it on. She sprays water at Tim.

"Hey, stop that!" Tim says. He is wet and cold.

"Come on, Tim. It is like the pool. It is fun." Mia says. She smiles and sprays more water.

Tim is angry. He does not like Mia's idea. He grabs the hose from Mia. He sprays water at Mia.

"Hey, stop that!" Mia says. She is wet and cold too.

They spray water at each other. They do not see the big kids come out of the pool. The big kids are angry. They see Tim and Mia with the hose. They want the hose.

"Hey, give us the hose. It is ours." One big kid says. He snatches the hose from Tim.

"Hey, that is not fair. We were playing with it." Tim says. He tries to get the hose back.

The big kids push Tim and Mia away. They spray water at them. They laugh and call them names.

Tim and Mia are scared and sad. They run to Tim's mom. They tell her what happened.

Tim's mom is sorry. She hugs Tim and Mia. She says, "I am sorry, Tim and Mia. The big kids were mean to you. You did nothing wrong. You just wanted to have fun. But you should not play with the hose. It is not yours. It is for the pool. Next time, we will find another place to play. A place where you can swim and slide and be happy."

Tim and Mia nod. They are still wet and cold. But they feel better. They are still friends. They say, "Thank you, mom. We love you."

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. One day, Lily sees a big red truck in Ben's yard. She wants to play with it.

"Can I borrow your truck, Ben?" Lily asks.

"OK, but only for a little while. It is my favorite truck," Ben says.

Lily takes the truck and drives it around the grass. She makes loud noises like a real truck. She is very happy.

But then, a nosy cat comes out of the bushes. The cat sees the truck and runs after it. The cat jumps on the truck and scratches it with its claws. Lily is scared and angry.

"Go away, cat! This is not your truck!" Lily shouts.

The cat does not listen. It keeps scratching the truck. Lily tries to pull the truck away, but the cat is too strong. The truck's tire pops and the air comes out. The truck stops moving.

Lily starts to cry. She broke Ben's truck. She does not know what to do.

Ben hears Lily crying and runs to her. He sees the cat, the truck and the tire.

"What happened, Lily?" Ben asks.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I wanted to play with your truck, but the cat came and ruined it. It popped your tire. I did not mean to break it," Lily says.

Ben is sad and mad. He loves his truck. He wants to yell at Lily and the cat. But he sees that Lily is very sorry. He remembers that she is his friend.

"It's OK, Lily. It was an accident. The cat is very bad and nosy. Maybe we can fix the tire later. Do you want to play with something else?" Ben says.

Lily hugs Ben and says thank you. She is glad that Ben is not mad at her. She is still sad about the truck, but she is happy to have a good friend.

They go inside and play with blocks and dolls. They forget about the cat and the truck. They have fun together.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to run and jump and laugh. They saw a big hedge near the fence. The hedge had many green leaves and some red berries.

"Let's play hide and seek behind the hedge!" Lily said. "You count to ten and I will hide."

"OK!" Tom said. He closed his eyes and started to count. "One, two, three..."

Lily ran behind the hedge. She looked for a good spot to hide. She saw a hole under the hedge. She thought it was a good spot. She crawled into the hole.

"Four, five, six..." Tom counted.

Lily felt something soft and warm in the hole. She thought it was a blanket. She touched it with her hand. It was not a blanket. It was fur. She heard a growl. She saw two yellow eyes. It was not a hole. It was a den. It was a fox's den. And the fox was not happy.

"Seven, eight, nine..." Tom counted.

Lily screamed. The fox bit her hand. It was very painful. She tried to get out of the den. But the fox was fast. It grabbed her leg. It pulled her deeper into the den.

"Ten! Ready or not, here I come!" Tom said. He opened his eyes. He looked for Lily. He did not see her. He heard her scream. He heard the fox growl. He ran to the hedge. He saw the hole. He saw blood. He was scared.

"Help! Help!" Lily cried. "Tom, help me!"

Tom wanted to help Lily. But he did not know what to do. He was too small to fight the fox. He was too scared to go into the den. He ran to the house. He shouted for his mom. But his mom was not home. She had gone to the store. Tom was alone. He cried. He did not know if Lily was alive or dead. He did not know if the fox would come out and get him too. He wished he had never played behind the hedge. He wished he had never counted to ten. He wished he had never said OK.

Anna and Ben like to play with their model cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They make roads and bridges with sand and sticks in the backyard. Sometimes they pretend that their cars are racing or going on adventures.

One day, they find a big hole in the sand. They wonder what is inside. They decide to bury their cars in the hole and dig them out later. They think it will be fun to see who can find their cars first.

They take turns putting their cars in the hole and covering them with sand. They say goodbye to their cars and promise to come back soon. They go inside to have a snack and wash their hands.

After they finish their snack, they run back to the backyard. They are excited to dig up their cars. But when they get to the hole, they see something else. A big dog is lying on the sand, wagging its tail. It has dug up all their cars and is playing with them.

"Hey, that's our hole!" Anna says. "And those are our cars!"

The dog looks at them and barks. It does not want to share. It picks up a car in its mouth and runs away.

"Come back, dog!" Ben says. "Give us our cars!"

Anna and Ben chase the dog around the backyard. They try to get their cars back, but the dog is too fast and too strong. They get tired and sad. They think they have lost their cars forever.

Then they hear a voice. It is their neighbor, Mr. Lee. He is holding a leash. He sees the dog and the children.

"I'm sorry, kids," he says. "This is my dog, Spot. He escaped from his yard. He likes to dig and play with things. He didn't mean to be naughty. He was just curious."

He walks over to the dog and puts the leash on him. He tells the dog to drop the car. The dog obeys. He drops the car and licks Mr. Lee's face.

"Good boy, Spot," Mr. Lee says. "Now let's give the children their cars back. You have to be helpful, not harmful."

He helps Anna and Ben collect their cars. He checks if they are broken or dirty. He apologizes for the trouble. He says he will fill the hole and fix the sand.

Anna and Ben are happy to have their cars back. They are not angry at the dog anymore. They see that he is friendly and playful. They thank Mr. Lee for being helpful.

"Can we pet your dog?" Anna asks.

"Sure, you can," Mr. Lee says. "He likes to make new friends. Just be gentle and careful."

Anna and Ben pet the dog. The dog wags its tail and licks their hands. They laugh and smile. They think the dog is cute and funny.

They decide to share their cars with the dog. They let him chase them and fetch them. They have fun playing together. They learn to be helpful, not harmful.

"Wow, look at these toys!" Tom says. "They are so pretty and new. Can we play with them?"

"Yes, let's play!" Anna says. "I want the blue plane. It can fly high in the sky."

But then, a big boy comes. He sees the toys and wants them. He runs to the box and grabs the yellow ball and the green ring.

"Hey, these are mine!" he says. "I put them in the box. Give me the car and the plane too!"

"No, they are ours!" Tom says. "We found them first. You can't have them!"

He puts the ring on his finger and tries to take the car and the plane from Tom and Anna. But the ring is bitter. It hurts his finger and makes him feel bad. He cries and drops the toys.

"Ow, ow, ow!" he says. "The ring is bitter. It bites me. Take it off, take it off!"

Tom and Anna see the big boy cry. They feel sorry for him. They help him take off the ring and give him a hug.

"It's okay, don't cry," Anna says. "The ring is not nice. It doesn't give you power. It makes you mean and sad. You don't need the ring to be strong and smart. You can be strong and smart by being kind and sharing."

"Really?" the big boy says. "Can I be your friend? Can we play together?"

"Yes, you can," Tom says. "Let's play together. We can share the toys. We have enough for everyone."

They smile and play with the toys. They share the car, the plane, the ball, and the ring. They have more fun and laugh. The ring is not bitter anymore. It is shiny and happy. It likes to see them happy.

"Wow, look at this stone!" Lily said. "Can I have it?"

"OK, I promise to share my cookies with you," she said. She took the stone and smiled.

Sara and Ben were playing outside. They liked to run and jump and sing. They saw a big red mailbox near the road. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's open it and look," Sara said.

"No, we can't. It's not ours. It's for the mailman," Ben said.

But Sara did not listen. She ran to the mailbox and pulled the handle. It was hard to open. She used both hands and pushed with all her might. She opened the mailbox and saw some letters and a magazine.

"Wow, look at this!" Sara said. She took out the magazine and looked at the pictures. There were animals and cars and toys.

Ben followed Sara and looked at the mailbox. He saw that it was open. He felt scared.

"Sara, close it! Close it now! The mailman will be mad!" Ben said.

But Sara did not listen. She was too busy looking at the magazine. She liked the colors and the shapes. She wanted to keep it.

"No, I want to see more. It's mine now," Sara said.

Just then, they heard a loud honk. It was the mailman. He was driving his big blue truck. He saw the open mailbox and the magazine in Sara's hands. He was very grumpy.

"Hey, you kids! What are you doing? That's not your mailbox! That's not your magazine! Give it back to me!" the mailman shouted.

He got out of his truck and walked to Sara and Ben. He looked angry. He reached for the magazine.

Sara and Ben were scared. They did not want the mailman to yell at them. They did not want to get in trouble.

"Sorry, sorry, sorry!" Ben said. He quickly closed the mailbox and ran away.

Sara was still holding the magazine. She did not want to give it back. She liked it too much.

"No, no, no!" Sara said. She tried to run away too, but the mailman was faster. He grabbed the magazine from her hands.

"That's mine! That's mine!" Sara cried. She kicked and screamed.

The mailman was very grumpy. He did not like Sara and Ben. He did not like their game. He put the magazine back in the mailbox and locked it.

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I don't want to be mean. I want to be charming. I want to have real friends. I want to share and care. I want to make others happy. And that is a good way to live."

Her mom smiled and said, "That's right, Lily. That is a good way to live. And I'm proud of you. You are a charming girl. And you have a charming king. And I love you both very much."

The end.

Moral value: Being mean makes you unhappy and lonely. Being charming makes you happy and friendly.

She ran to her house and showed it to her mom. "Look, mom, I have a snowflake! It is the most beautiful thing in the world!"

Her mom smiled and said, "It is very beautiful, Lily, but you can't keep it forever. It will melt soon. You have to let it go."

Lily did not want to let it go. She said, "No, mom, I want to keep it. It is mine. It is my snowflake."

She put it in a jar and closed the lid. She put the jar on her shelf and looked at it every day. She thought it was still the same.

But it was not the same. It was melting slowly. It was losing its shape and sparkle. It was becoming a drop of water.

Lily did not notice. She was too busy playing with other things. She forgot about her snowflake.

One day, she remembered her snowflake and went to look at it. She was shocked. She saw only a drop of water in the jar. She cried and said, "Where is my snowflake? What happened to it?"

Her mom came and hugged her. She said, "I'm sorry, Lily, but your snowflake melted. It was not meant to be kept in a jar. It was meant to be free in the air. It had a life of its own. You should have let it go when you had the chance."

Lily felt sad and sorry. She said, "I'm sorry, mom, I did not know. I was selfish. I wanted to keep it for myself. I did not think about its life."

Her mom said, "It's okay, Lily, you learned a lesson. Sometimes, we have to let go of the things we love, because they have their own lives. We can enjoy them while they last, but we can't hold them forever. That is the way of the world."

Lily nodded and said, "I understand, mom. Thank you for teaching me. I will not be selfish again. I will let go of the things I love when they need to go."

She opened the jar and poured the water out. She said goodbye to her snowflake and thanked it for being so beautiful. She hoped it would find a new life somewhere else.

She felt a little sad, but also a little happy. She learned to respect the life of others. She learned to let go.

"Sara, I know you like to paint. But you have to be careful. Some things do not like to be painted. Some things may feel hurt or angry if you paint them. You have to ask before you paint something. You have to respect other things. Do you understand?"

Sara nodded. She said:

"I'm sorry, mom. I did not know. I was scared of the dog. I wanted to make it nice. But I made it mad. I will not paint the dog again. I will ask before I paint something. I will respect other things."

Mom smiled. She said:

"That's good, Sara. I'm proud of you. You learned a lesson today. Painting is fun, but it is also a responsibility. You have to use your paints wisely and kindly. Now, let's go and find something else to paint. Something that likes to be painted. How about a rainbow?"

Anna and Ben do not understand. They are scared. They drop the phone and run away.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big flag on a pole. The flag is red and white and blue. It has stars and stripes.

"Wow, look at the flag!" Tom says. "It is so pretty!"

"I want to touch it," Mia says. "Can we get it?"

Tom and Mia run to the pole. They try to reach the flag, but it is too high. They jump and stretch, but they cannot touch it.

"Let's get a stick," Tom says. "Maybe we can poke the flag."

They find a stick on the ground. They try to poke the flag, but the stick is too short. They push and pull, but they cannot poke it.

"Let's get a chair," Mia says. "Maybe we can climb the pole."

They find a chair near a bench. They try to drag the chair, but it is too heavy. They push and pull, but they cannot drag it.

"Let's give up," Tom says. "We can't get the flag."

They drop the stick and the chair. They walk away from the pole. They are sad and tired.

A man sees them. He is wearing a uniform. He has a badge and a hat. He is a guard. He is angry.

"Hey, you two!" he shouts. "What are you doing with the flag?"

Tom and Mia are scared. They stop and look at the man.

"We are sorry, sir," Tom says. "We just wanted to touch the flag."

"We like the flag," Mia says. "It is so pretty."

The man walks to them. He looks at the stick and the chair. He looks at the flag. He looks at Tom and Mia.

He sighs. He is not angry anymore. He is kind.

"I know you like the flag," he says. "But you can't touch it. It is not a toy. It is a symbol. It means something important."

"What does it mean?" Tom asks.

"It means freedom and justice and courage," the man says. "It means we are proud of our country and our people. It means we respect and honor those who protect us and serve us."

Tom and Mia nod. They understand a little bit.

"Can we look at the flag?" Tom asks.

"Of course you can," the man says. "You can look at it and admire it and learn from it. But you can't touch it or poke it or climb it. That is not respectful. That is not nice."

Tom and Mia nod again. They are sorry. They did not know.

"Can we say sorry to the flag?" Mia asks.

The man smiles. He is touched.

"That is very sweet of you," he says. "Yes, you can say sorry to the flag. And then you can say thank you to the flag. And then you can wave to the flag. And then you can go and play."

Tom and Mia do what the man says. They say sorry to the flag. They say thank you to the flag. They wave to the flag. They feel better.

They go and play. They have fun. They are friends.

They never forget the flag. They never forget the man. They never forget what he taught them.

The moral of the story is: vegetables are important for our health and well-being, and we should not judge them by their appearance.

He took out his new toy from his backpack and showed it to Lily. Lily thought it was cute, but she also knew it was not a good idea to give it to the crocodiles.

"Ben, don't do that. The crocodiles will grab your toy and bite it. They might even grab your hand and hurt you. You have to keep your toy safe," Lily said.

But Ben did not listen. He wanted to see what the crocodiles would do. He climbed on the fence and threw his toy into the pond. The toy landed with a splash and squeaked loudly.

One of the crocodiles heard the noise and opened its eyes. It saw the toy floating on the water and thought it was a tasty snack. It swam quickly towards the toy and grabbed it with its mouth. It crunched the toy and made it stop squeaking.

Ben gasped and cried. He had lost his new toy. He wished he had listened to Lily and Mom. He felt very sorry and sad.

The crocodile saw them and smiled. He thought, "What a tasty snack!" He swam closer and closer to them.

The frog and the mouse thought they were doomed. They closed their eyes and waited for the end.

But then, something happened. The crocodile sneezed. He sneezed very loud and hard. He sneezed so much that he let go of the frog and the mouse. He sneezed so much that he could not see or hear anything.

The frog and the mouse saw their chance. They quickly swam to the shore and ran to a safe place. They were very lucky and happy.

They looked at the crocodile. He was still sneezing. He looked very silly and miserable.

The frog and the mouse realized that the crocodile had sneezed because of the swamp. The swamp had many plants and animals. Some of them made the crocodile allergic. He could not stand the swamp.

The frog and the mouse learned a lesson. They learned that the swamp was their home and their friend. They learned that the swamp protected them from the fierce crocodile. They learned to love and respect the swamp.

They also learned to be careful and watchful. They learned to avoid the crocodile and other dangers. They learned to stick together and help each other.

They thanked the swamp and each other. They hugged and smiled. They continued to play in the swamp. They were happy and safe.

The fox said, "Sure, I can help you. But you have to share them with me. Half for you and half for me. Deal?"

The monkey agreed. He climbed the tree and picked some bananas. He threw them down to the fox. But the fox was greedy and ignorant. He did not want to share. He hid some bananas under a bush. He said, "Here are your bananas, monkey. I have split them fairly. See?"

The monkey came down from the tree. He saw the bananas on the ground. He counted them. He said, "Wait a minute, fox. These are not half. You have more than me. Where are the rest of the bananas?"

The fox lied. He said, "There are no more bananas, monkey. The tree was empty. You are lucky I gave you some. Now stop complaining and eat them."

The monkey was not fooled. He saw the bush moving. He said, "You are lying, fox. You have hidden some bananas under the bush. You are not a good friend. You are selfish and mean. Give me my bananas, or I will tell the lion."

The fox was scared. He did not want to face the lion. He said, "No, no, no, monkey. Don't tell the lion. I was just joking. Here are your bananas. Take them. I am sorry. Please forgive me."

The monkey took his bananas. He said, "You should be sorry, fox. You should not lie and cheat. You should be honest and fair. Next time, I will not trust you. Now go away and leave me alone."

At the girl's house, the chicken was put in a cage. The girl would come and visit the chicken every day and give it some food. But one day, the girl forgot to give the chicken food. The chicken was very hungry and started to cry. But no one heard the chicken's cry.

The next day, the girl found the little gray chicken dead in the cage. The girl was very sad and realized that she should have never taken the chicken away from its home. From that day on, the girl promised to never take an animal away from its home again.

"Can we help you, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Look, we washed the rice for you, Mom!" Lily shouted.

"Thank you, my darlings. You are very helpful. Let me see the rice." Mom said as she came back.

"No, no, no! This is not good! This is very bad! You threw away the good rice and kept the bad rice! The bad rice has bugs in it! Bugs can make you sick! You can't eat this rice!" Mom yelled.

"But we are hungry, Mom. We want to eat rice. We don't see any bugs. We only see rice." Lily said.

"Please, Mom. We are sorry. We didn't know. We thought they were peas. We don't like peas." Ben said.

Mom shook her head. She did not know what to do. She had no more rice in the house. She had no money to buy more rice. She had no time to go to the store. She had to go to work soon. She had no choice. She had to cook the bad rice for Lily and Ben.

She was wrong.

Max was scared. He did not know where to go. Then, he remembered what Tim said. Max learned to listen to his friend. He found his way back to the gate. Tim was happy to see Max.

Max said, "I am sorry, Tim. I will listen to you next time." Tim smiled and said, "That's okay, Max. We all learn from our mistakes."

The moral of the story is to listen to our friends and learn from our mistakes.

Lila and Ben like to play with balls. They have many balls of different colors and sizes. They like to roll them, throw them, catch them, and bounce them.

One day, they find a new ball in the park. It is big and green and hard. It has many lines on it. Lila and Ben wonder what it is.

"Is it a ball?" Lila asks.

"I don't know. Let's try to roll it," Ben says.

They push the ball with their hands, but it does not roll. It is too heavy and rough. They try to kick it, but it hurts their feet. It does not bounce. They try to lift it, but it is too big. They cannot catch it.

"What is this?" Lila says. "It is not a fun ball."

"Maybe it is not a ball at all," Ben says. "Maybe it is something else."

They look around and see a man sitting on a bench. He has a hat and a book. He looks kind and patient.

"Excuse me, sir," Lila says. "Do you know what this is?"

The man smiles and puts down his book. He walks over to them and looks at the ball.

"That is not a ball, my dear," he says. "That is a coconut. It is a fruit that grows on a palm tree. It has water and meat inside. You can drink and eat it, but you have to open it first."

"A coconut?" Lila and Ben say. "How do you open it?"

The man shows them how to find the eyes and the mouth of the coconut. He takes a rock and hits the coconut hard. It cracks and splits. He gives them each a half. They see the white meat and the clear water.

"Wow, thank you, sir," Lila and Ben say. "Can we try it?"

"Of course, you can," the man says. "But be careful, it might be a bit hard and sweet."

Lila and Ben sip the water and bite the meat. They like it. It is different from any ball they have ever played with. They thank the man again and share the coconut with him. They learn a new word and a new fruit. They are happy.

"Here, use this," she says. "It will help you push the bulb out."

Ben takes the shovel and puts it under the bulb. He pushes with all his might. The bulb pops out of the ground and flies into the air.

"Wow!" Anna and Ben say. "You did it!"

They catch the bulb and look at it. It has a green stem and a purple flower on top. It is very pretty.

"It is a flower!" Anna says. "A beautiful flower. You are very smart, Ben."

"Thank you, Anna," Ben says. "You are very kind. Let's plant it again and watch it grow."

He used his loudspeaker and said, "Attention, attention. We have a lost child here. Her name is Lily. She has brown hair and a pink dress. She wandered away from her mom at the slide. If you are her mom, please come to the park ranger station. Thank you."

Her mom said, "I love you too, Lily. Now let's go home. You need a lecture and a nap."

"No, you're not, I'm faster than you!" Sam said.

They pushed their cars harder and harder, until they reached the fence. There was a big sign on the fence that said "STOP". Lily and Sam did not know what it meant, but they thought it looked important.

They paused their cars and looked at the sign. They saw a man on the other side of the fence. He was wearing a yellow hat and a orange vest. He had a big machine that made a loud noise. He was digging a hole in the ground.

"Hello, what are you doing?" Lily asked.

"Hello, I'm working. I'm digging a hole for a new pipe," the man said.

"What is a pipe?" Sam asked.

"A pipe is a thing that carries water or gas or other stuff. It goes under the ground or inside the walls," the man said.

"Why do you need a new pipe?" Lily asked.

"Because the old pipe is broken. It has a crack and it leaks. That's bad. It can make the water or gas or other stuff go where it shouldn't. That can be dangerous," the man said.

Lily and Sam did not understand everything the man said, but they understood that he was doing something important and hard. They wanted to learn more.

"Can you teach us how to dig a hole?" Sam asked.

"Sorry, I can't. This is not a game. This is a job. You need special tools and skills and safety rules. You can't play here. It's too hot and noisy and dirty. You might get hurt," the man said.

Lily and Sam felt sad and curious. They wanted to play with the big machine and the hole and the pipe. They thought it looked fun and cool.

"Please, can we just watch?" Lily asked.

"OK, you can watch, but only from a distance. And you have to listen to me. If I say stop, you have to stop. If I say go, you have to go. Do you understand?" the man said.

Lily and Sam nodded. They agreed to follow the man's rules. They moved their cars away from the fence and sat on the grass. They watched the man work. They asked him questions. He answered them. He taught them some new words and facts. They learned a lot.

They forgot about their cars and their race. They had a new game. They pretended they were workers too. They dug holes and fixed pipes and wore hats and vests. They had fun. They made friends. As she continued to walk, she heard a loud noise that made her ears feel deaf. It was a motorcycle speeding by, making a lot of noise. Lily covered her ears and waited for it to pass. She realized that sometimes things can be fast and loud, but it's important to stay safe and be careful.

She learned a valuable lesson that day - don't trust everything that makes you curious!

Once upon a time there was a zebra. It was very dull. It spent its days walking across the savannah.

The monkey was in a hurry. It ran around the zebra three times before climbing on to its back. The monkey chattered something and waved a stick around. 

The zebra started to walk. They travelled across the landscape until it was getting dark. Then the zebra paused again. 

The monkey jumped off and said 'thank you'. And with that, it raced off into the night. 

The zebra was confused but it shuffled home to its herd. From then on, it always paused when it heard the sound of a pesky little monkey!

Once upon a time there was a boy who loved to explore. One day he wandered out of his backyard and into a deep, dark forest. As he walked further, he saw something up ahead. He agreed. 

The tuna ran around, playing tag with the boy. Suddenly the tuna stopped and pointed to a clearing in the forest. "Look over there! There is danger lurking in the trees", the tuna said. Just then, a loud snarl came from the darkness. The boy was very scared, but the tuna stepped forward and offered to protect the boy. 

The tuna shouted to the darkness and the snarl stopped. The tuna waved its fins and created a safe path. The boy followed safely and soon they were outside of the dangerous forest. The boy thanked the tuna, and the tuna swam away. 

The boy had learned a lesson that day: always be brave and never give up.

After the vet visit, Lily and Max went back to the park. They saw some other kids playing a game of tag. Lily asked Max if he wanted to play, and Max barked happily. They joined the game, and Max ran so fast that he won! Lily was proud of her dependable dog.

Anna and her dad jog closer to the dog. The dog stops barking. He wags his tail. He licks Anna's face. Anna giggles. She says, "Hello, Max. You are a nice dog. Do you want to jog with us?"

The dog's owner comes. He is a man with a hat. He says, "Sorry, he is very quick. He likes to run and play. He is a tidy dog. He does not make a mess. He is my best friend. His name is Max."

Anna and her dad say hello to the man. They say they like Max. They ask if they can jog with them. The man says yes. They jog together in the park. They have fun. Anna and Max become friends. Anna is not scared anymore. She likes to jog with her dad and Max.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a man with a camera. He is taking photos of the flowers and the birds.

"Look, Ben, he has a camera!" Sara says. "I want to see the photos."

"Me too," Ben says. "Let's go and ask him."

They run to the man and say hello. The man smiles and says hello back.

"Can we see your photos?" Sara asks.

"Sure, you can," the man says. "I have a camera that shows the photos on a screen. Do you want to see?"

"Yes, please," Sara and Ben say.

The man shows them the screen. They see many photos of the park. They see yellow flowers, red flowers, blue flowers. They see a bird with a long tail, a bird with a short tail, a bird with a big beak. They see a squirrel, a dog, a cat.

"Wow, these are pretty photos," Sara says.

"Yes, I do," Sara says. "I like to look at everything."

"Me too," Ben says. "I like to look at you, Sara. You are attractive."

Sara blushes and smiles. The man laughs and says, "You are sweet, Ben. Do you want to take a photo with Sara?"

"Yes, please," Ben says.

The man takes out another camera. He says, "This is a camera that prints the photos. Do you want to have a photo?"

"Yes, please," Sara and Ben say.

The man tells them to stand together and smile. He takes a photo of them. He gives them the photo. They see themselves on the photo. They are smiling and holding hands.

"Thank you, mister," Sara and Ben say.

"You are welcome, kids," the man says. "You are very nice and friendly. Have fun in the park."

Sara and Ben say goodbye to the man. They run to the swings. They look at the photo. They are happy. They are friends.

Lily and Tom were twins. They liked to play with their toys in the living room. But they did not like to share. They always fought over who got the best toy.

One day, their mom brought home a new baby. She said, "This is your little brother, Sam. He is an infant. He is very small and needs a lot of love and care. You have to be gentle and kind to him."

Lily and Tom were curious. They wanted to see the infant. But they also wanted to play with their toys. They did not listen to their mom. They ran to the crib and grabbed the infant's blanket, hat, and pacifier. They said, "These are our toys now. We want to play with them."

They pulled and tugged at the infant's things. They made him cry. They did not care. They were having fun. They ran around the living room and scattered the infant's things everywhere. They threw them on the floor, on the couch, and on the table.

Their mom heard the noise and the crying. She was very angry. She came to the living room and saw the mess. She said, "Lily and Tom, what have you done? You are very naughty and selfish. You have hurt your little brother and made a big mess. You are not playing with your toys. You are playing with his things. They are not toys. They are important for him. He needs them to be warm and comfortable and happy. You have to give them back to him right now. And you have to say sorry to him. And you have to help me clean up this mess. Or you will have no toys at all."

Lily and Tom realized they had been very stupid. They felt sorry for their little brother. They said, "We are sorry, Sam. We are sorry, mom. We will give back his things. We will help you clean up. We will be gentle and kind to him. We will share our toys with him. We love him."

Their mom smiled. She said, "That's good. I'm glad you learned your lesson. Sharing is caring. And caring is loving. And loving is what makes a family happy."

Lily loved to grow tomatoes in her garden. She watered them every day and sang to them. She was very proud of her red and juicy tomatoes. She wanted to share them with her friends.

One day, she picked some tomatoes and put them in a basket. She walked to the park where her friends were playing. She saw Ben, Mia and Sam on the swings. She waved to them and said, "Look, I have tomatoes for you!"

Her friends were happy to see her and her tomatoes. They ran to her and took some from the basket. They thanked her and said, "You are very kind, Lily. Your tomatoes are delicious!"

But then, they saw a big dog coming towards them. The dog was barking and growling. It looked dangerous. It wanted to eat the tomatoes and maybe the children too. The children were scared and did not know what to do.

Lily had an idea. She said, "Don't be afraid. We can scare the dog away. Let's throw the tomatoes at the dog and make loud noises. Then the dog will run away."

The children agreed and did what Lily said. They threw the tomatoes at the dog and shouted, "Go away, dog! Go away!" The dog was surprised and afraid. It did not like the tomatoes and the noises. It turned around and ran away.

The children were happy and relieved. They hugged each other and said, "We did it! We are brave and smart!" They looked at Lily and said, "You are our hero, Lily. You saved us from the dog. You are the best!"

They all applauded Lily and cheered for her. Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, friends. I'm glad you are safe. But I'm sorry we wasted the tomatoes. They were for you."

Her friends said, "Don't be sorry, Lily. The tomatoes were not wasted. They helped us to get rid of the dog. They were more than food. They were weapons!"

They all laughed and said, "You are right, Lily. The tomatoes were weapons. But they were also gifts. Gifts of love and friendship. We love you, Lily. And we love your tomatoes!"

The moral of the story is: Be generous and share what you have with others. Be brave and use what you have to face problems. Be grateful and appreciate what you have and what others give you.

One night, Anna and Ben hear a noise outside the tent. It sounds like a growl. Anna is scared. She hugs her teddy bear. Ben is curious. He wants to see what it is.

"Ben, don't go!" Anna whispers. "It might be a big bad animal!"

Ben does not listen. He zips the tent and peeks out. He sees a shadow moving in the dark. He grabs the lamp and shines it at the shadow. He gasps.

"Anna, look!" he says. "It is a dog!"

Anna looks out too. She sees a dog with brown fur and a wagging tail. It is not a big bad animal. It is a friendly dog. The dog sees the lamp and barks. It runs towards the tent.

"What is going on?" Mom asks. She sees Ben and Anna running after the dog with the lamp.

"They are playing with a dog," Dad says. He laughs. He gets out of the tent and joins them.

The dog is fast. It runs to the lake. It drops the lamp in the water. The lamp goes out. The dog jumps in the water. It splashes and swims.

"Oops, there goes the lamp," Ben says. He is sad. He liked the lamp.

"Maybe we can get another one," Anna says. She is not sad. She liked the dog.

Mom and Dad hug Ben and Anna. They are happy. They liked the camping.

Lily was a brown dog who loved to play with her ball. She would run and jump and catch the ball in her mouth. She was very happy.

One day, she saw a big cat in the garden. The cat had a shiny bell on its neck. Lily wanted to play with the cat and the bell. She ran towards the cat with her ball in her mouth.

The cat did not want to play with Lily. The cat was scared of the big dog. The cat hissed and scratched at Lily. Lily felt a sharp pain in her ear. She dropped the ball and cried.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily said. "Why did you hurt me? I just wanted to play!"

The cat said, "Go away, dog! You are too loud and too rough. You scared me with your ball. This is my bell, not yours. Leave me alone!"

Lily was sad and angry. She wanted to bite the cat and take the bell. But then she remembered what her mom had taught her. She said, "I'm sorry, cat. I didn't mean to scare you. I should have asked you first. Can we be friends?"

The cat was surprised. He saw that Lily was not a bad dog. He said, "I'm sorry, too, dog. I didn't mean to hurt you. I was afraid of you. Maybe we can be friends. But please, don't chase me or try to take my bell. Can you release your ball and play with something else?"

Lily nodded. She released her ball and found a stick. She said, "OK, cat. I will play with the stick. You can keep your bell. Maybe we can share sometimes."

The cat smiled. He said, "OK, dog. I will play with the bell. You can keep your stick. Maybe we can share sometimes."

Lily and the cat became friends. They learned to respect each other and their things. They had fun playing in the garden.

The moral of the story is: Be kind and polite to others, even if they are different from you. Don't take what is not yours without asking. Share and play nicely. You can make new friends.

Anna likes to write. She has a big book and a red pen. She writes her name, her age, and her favorite things. She writes about her cat, her doll, and her bike.

One day, she goes to the park with her mom. She sees a big oak tree. It has many leaves and acorns. She wants to write about the tree. She asks her mom for her book and pen.

"Can I write here, mom?" she says.

"Sure, Anna. But be careful. Don't go too far from me," her mom says.

Anna sits under the tree. She writes "oak" on her book. She draws a picture of the tree. She sees a little squirrel on a branch. It has a bushy tail and a nut in its mouth. She writes "squirrel" and draws it too.

She hears a noise. She looks up. She sees another squirrel. It is bigger than the first one. It jumps from the branch to the ground. It runs towards Anna. It wants her pen.

"Hey, that's mine!" Anna says.

She holds her pen tight. The squirrel tries to grab it. It scratches Anna's hand. Anna cries.

"Mom, help!" she says.

Her mom hears her. She runs to her. She sees the squirrel and the pen. She scares the squirrel away. She hugs Anna.

"Are you okay, Anna?" she says.

"It hurts, mom. The squirrel was mean. It wanted my pen," Anna says.

"I'm sorry, Anna. Let me see your hand. It's just a little scratch. It will be better soon. Here, have a band-aid," her mom says.

She puts a band-aid on Anna's hand. She kisses it. She gives Anna her pen back.

"Thank you, mom. I love you," Anna says.

"I love you too, Anna. Do you want to go home now?" her mom says.

"No, mom. I want to write more. But not about squirrels. They are bad," Anna says.

"Okay, Anna. You can write more. But stay close to me. And be careful of squirrels. They are not bad. They are just hungry and curious," her mom says.

Anna nods. She writes more on her book. She writes about her mom, her hand, and her band-aid. She is happy. She likes to write.

"What is that?" Sam said.

As he sailed away, Sam knew he'd had a great adventure. He truly had ended the day with a smile.

Frustrated that the butterfly was getting away, Lily called out to it with determination.

"Wait for me!" she shouted.

The butterfly paused and turned to look at Lily. Then, it flew back and landed on her shoulder. It blinked at her steadily before taking off again. Lily grinned with delight and ran east.

The butterfly continued to guide Lily, always keeping an eye on her and blinking its approval. With each step, they ventured east. Eventually, they stopped together at the edge of a lake. Lily watched the butterfly flutter away in the sunset and sighed happily. Thanks to her persistent pursuit and the butterfly's help, Lily had come a long way east!

Lila said, "I want to talk to you. I want to know more about you. What do you like to do?"

They decide to work hard and clean up every day. They put the blocks in the bin, the books on the shelf, the crayons in the box, and the puzzles in the drawer. They help each other and say please and thank you. They make Miss Lee happy and proud.

One day, Sara's big brother Tom came into her room. He was angry because Sara had taken his toy car. He wanted to make Sara sorry. He saw Lily on Sara's bed and grabbed her. He said, "This is your stupid doll, right? Well, now it's mine!"

One day, she saw a new poppy in her garden. It was the biggest and prettiest of all. It had a bright yellow center and a long stem. Lily was very happy. She ran to her mom and said, "Mom, look! I have a new poppy! Can I pick it and put it in a vase?"

Lily said, "I will, Mom. I love the poppy. It is my best friend." She put the vase on the table and went to play with her toys.

The next day, Lily woke up and ran to the table. She wanted to see the poppy and say good morning. But when she got there, she saw that the vase was empty. The poppy was gone. Lily was very sad. She cried and said, "Where is my poppy? Who took it?"

Mom came and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. But I told you, the poppy was magic. It could only stay for one day. After that, it had to go back to the garden. It was a gift, not a toy. You have to let it go."

Lily said, "But I loved it, Mom. I was kind and gentle to it. Why did it vanish?"

Mom said, "You were kind and gentle to it, Lily. But you were not kind and gentle to the other poppies. You picked them all and threw them away. You did not water them or sing to them. You did not care for them. You only cared for the magic poppy. That was not fair. The poppies were sad and angry. They asked the magic poppy to leave. And it did."

Lily realized that she had been mean and rough to the other poppies. She felt sorry and ashamed. She said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I'm sorry, poppies. I was wrong. I should have loved you all. Can I make it up to you?"

Mom said, "Yes, Lily. You can. You can plant new seeds and water them and sing to them. You can be kind and gentle to them. Maybe, one day, they will grow big and pretty. And maybe, one day, another magic poppy will come. And maybe, it will grant you another wish. But only if you are kind and gentle. Do you understand?"

Lily said, "Yes, Mom. I understand. I will be kind and gentle. I will love the poppies. Thank you, Mom. Thank you, poppies." She hugged her mom and went to the garden. She planted new seeds and watered them and sang to them. She hoped they would grow big and pretty. And she hoped that another magic poppy would come. And she hoped that it would be her friend.

Lily was afraid of thunder. She did not like the loud noise and the dark sky. She always hid under her bed when it rained and thundered. She wished the thunder would go away.

One day, she saw a book about thunder on the shelf. She was curious and wanted to learn more. She asked her mom if she could read the book. Her mom said yes and helped her open the book. The book had many pictures and words. Lily liked the pictures, but some of the words were hard.

"Mom, what is this word?" Lily asked, pointing to a word on the page.

"That is 'fragile', dear. It means something that can break easily, like a glass or a flower," her mom explained.

"Oh, I see. And what is this word?" Lily asked, pointing to another word.

"That is 'lightning', dear. It is a bright flash of light that comes from the sky when it thunders. It is very fast and powerful," her mom said.

"Wow, that sounds scary. Does lightning hurt?" Lily asked, feeling worried.

"Sometimes, it can hurt, if it hits something or someone. But it is very rare and we are safe inside our house. We have a roof and walls that protect us from the rain and the thunder and the lightning," her mom assured her.

Lily felt a little better, but she was still afraid. She hugged her mom and the book. She hoped the thunder would stop soon.

Suddenly, there was a loud bang and a flash of light. Lily screamed and dropped the book. The book fell on the floor and the pages tore. Lily felt sad and scared. She had broken the fragile book.

"Mom, I'm sorry, I broke the book!" Lily cried.

Her mom hugged her and comforted her. "It's okay, sweetie, it was an accident. The book is not as important as you. You are my precious and brave girl. I love you, no matter what," her mom said.

Lily felt loved and calm. She said sorry to the book and thanked her mom. She learned that thunder was not so bad, after all. She also learned to be careful with fragile things. She smiled and cuddled with her mom and the book. The thunder was still loud, but she was not afraid anymore.

The horse smiled and said, "No, I'm sorry. I want a husband with strong muscles and you don't have them." 

Bob was very disappointed, but he understood what the horse was saying. So, he decided to work very hard and exercise every day. 

Months went by, and Bob became much stronger. Eventually he had lots of muscles! So he went back to the horse's house and asked her to marry him. The horse was impressed with all the hard work Bob had put in, and she said yes.

So Bob and the horse got married and they lived together very happily ever after.

The moral of the story is that with hard work and dedication, anything is possible.

So, he started looking everywhere. He looked in the trees, he looked in the rocks, he looked through the bushes, but he couldn't find the fireplace he was looking for.

Just then, he saw a rabbit hopping through the forest. The bear said, "Hello there! Can you help me? I'm looking for a fireplace."

The rabbit replied, "Oh, why yes I can! Don't worry, I know just the place for you. Follow me!"

So, the bear followed the rabbit deep into the woods until they finally came to a lovely little cottage with a big, warm fireplace inside.

The bear said, "Thank you so much for your help!"

"It was no problem!" the bunny said with a smile. "It's what honest friends do!"

Startled, Ben gasped. He slowly peered around the room, feeling a little frightened. Suddenly, he heard the noise again - "Hey there!", came a voice from inside the cube tower. 

Ben looked up to see a friendly little creature at the top of the tower. It was a pink-spotted frog with a wide grin. 

Ben was very relieved and started to laugh. He thanked the frog for helping him organize the cubes. The frog smiled back and responded, "It was my pleasure" and hopped away. 

Ben smiled and continued to play, feeling very glad that he was no longer frightened.

Mia was very curious, so she walked closer to take a look. She noticed that the onion was pulsing with a pink light. She reached out her hand and suddenly the onion grew big and started to hum loudly. Mia wanted to pick it up but it felt too hot.

"You shouldn't touch it," a voice whispered.
Mia looked around and saw a strange old man standing nearby. "Oh hello!" she said. The man said, "That onion is very dangerous. It feeds on negative energy. If you touch it, it will take away your troubles and give you a new kind of pain."

Mia was a bit scared, so she stepped away from the glowing onion. "Thank you for warning me," she said. But it was too late. That night, Matt's dad noticed something was wrong. He asked Matt what was wrong and Matt explained everything.

Later that night, Matt went to the park to find Lily and Jack playing together. Matt got angry and yelled at them. Lily was scared of Matt and ran away.

Jack and Matt started to fight and soon there was no peace in the park. The police soon arrived and everyone had to go home. The two friends never talked again and peace was gone from the park forever.

When they got it home, Daddy plugged in the fridge, and then plugged it in the wall. Mommy then opened the door and put things inside. 

The little girl was curious. She asked, "What are you doing?"

Mommy said, "We are putting food in the fridge so it does not spoil."

Daddy closed the door and said, "We're finished."

Mommy and Daddy went outside to play with the little girl. She was very happy because they had a nice fridge.

John was walking down the street. He looked up and noticed a big, red mailbox. He ran up to it and said, "Wow, this mailbox is so smart!" He opened the mailbox and there was a letter inside. He was very excited and started to guess what the letter said.

"Do you think the letter is from my mommy?" He asked his friend.
"I'm not sure - but it could be," his friend said.

So John carefully opened the letter. Inside there was a hug, and a picture of John's mommy. John smiled from ear to ear.

"You were so smart to guess that the letter was from your mommy!" His friend said.

John was so happy. With the help of his smart eyes, he had found an amazing surprise in the mailbox.

Once upon a time, there lived a boy named Max in a small village at the edge of a forest. Every morning, Max would go to the forest and collect wood.

One day, while Max was in the forest, he heard a voice calling out to him.

"Max! I need your help!" 

Max was very troubled. He had no idea who the voice belonged to. He looked around but didn't see anyone. He was about to turn back when the voice spoke to him again.

"Max, I need your help to deliver something to the people of the village. Will you help me?" 

Max asked who the voice belonged to, and he saw a big white owl in the tree above him. The owl said, "I am the Spirit of the Forest. I need your help to deliver a message to the villagers. Will you help me, Max?" 

Max was really scared, but he agreed to help. The Spirit gave him the message and told him to deliver it to the villagers. 

That night, the villagers were surprised when they heard the news. The Spirit had warned them of a dangerous storm coming their way. The villagers were prepared and the storm passed without any harm.

Max was happy that he had been able to help the Spirit of the Forest, and the villagers were thankful for his help. They all thanked Max for being brave and delivering the important message.

Jenny was walking in the land with her mom. As they walked, Jenny noticed the bright green grass, the trees with their leaves rustling in the breeze and the sunshine glinting off of the river. She smiled with delight. 

Jenny's mom stopped suddenly and put her hand up. "What is it Mommy?" asked Jenny curiously. 

Mom pointed ahead and revealed a careless rabbit hopping around in the grass. "Oh look" she said with a bright smile. 

Jenny loved animals, so she eagerly approached the rabbit, but just as she was about to touch him, the rabbit hopped into a nearby bush. Jenny looked disappointed, but her Mom held her hand tight and they continued their walk. Jenny was content with the memory of the rabbit and the land around her.

"Oh no, that was scary!" said the rabbit.

Lily's mom saw them fighting and told them to listen. She said that sharing is very important. So, Lily and Tim decided to share their clay and play together. They made new friends and had lots of fun.

Lily and Max gathered the pretty rocks with the big bird. They all became friends and played on the hill together.

When Lily and Max went outside to play, Lily showed him her squash plant. Max thought it was really cool and asked if he could borrow some seeds to plant in his own garden. Lily said yes and gave him some.

Later, when it was time for Max to go home, Lily remembered her promise to her mom. She checked the box of toys and saw that the important toy was missing. She asked Max if he had seen it and he remembered that he had borrowed it to play with. He quickly went to get it and returned it to Lily.

Lily was happy that Max was honest and returned the important toy. She knew she could trust him to borrow things in the future.

The bee was surprised but he didn't fly away. He just watched as a little girl came out of the house and started to rock the rock quickly. She was laughing, having so much fun!

The bee was happy and he stayed to enjoy the show. He watched as the little girl rocked the big rock. She was so alert and looked around to make sure the bee was still there. The bee smiled and waved goodbye as the little girl went back into the house.

Suddenly, a very rude ghost appeared. The ghost said, "No - I won't come and talk to you!" 

Jane was a bit sad but then she remembered something. She had a special whistle that would make the ghost obedient. So, she took out the whistle, blew it really loudly, and said, "Please ghost - I request that you come and talk to me!"

Tim and Kim ran to the old man. They wanted to see what he had. They grabbed the books, the puzzles, and the crayons. They did not say thank you or ask nicely. They just took what they wanted and ran away.

The old man was sad. He said, "Why are you so rude? Don't you know how to share? Sharing is caring. If you share, you will have more friends and more fun."

But Tim and Kim did not listen. They shut their ears and their mouths. They did not care about the old man or the other kids. They just wanted to play with their new toys.

Tim and Kim nodded. They said, "Thank you, sir. We will try to share. We want to have more friends and more fun."

The old man was happy. He said, "You see, children. Sharing is caring. If you share, you will have more friends and more fun. And you will also make me happy."

Max hugged her. He was still angry, but he loved her. He hoped mom would not be mad at them for messing up the cake. He hoped Lily would learn her lesson. He hoped the flame would not spoil mom's birthday.

As Lily played with the puppy, she felt something bite her arm. It was a mosquito! She swatted it away and made sure to put on bug spray to keep the mosquitoes away. 

After playing with the puppy for a while, Lily gave it back to its owner and went inside to rest. She was happy to have made a new friend and to have borrowed such an adorable puppy. The end.

She wanted to show her picture to her mom. She called, "Mom, mom, look at my picture!" But her mom did not answer. She called again, "Mom, mom, where are you?" But her mom did not answer.

She got up from her desk and went to look for her mom. She left her pencils on the floor. She did not put them back in the box.

She went to the kitchen, but her mom was not there. She went to the living room, but her mom was not there. She went to the bedroom, but her mom was not there.

She was sad and confused. Where was her mom?

Her mom looked up and smiled. She saw Lily holding her picture. She said, "Lily, I'm so proud of you. You drew a beautiful picture of our family. Come here and show me."

Lily ran to her mom and hugged her. She showed her the picture and explained who was who. Her mom praised her and kissed her.

She said, "Lily, you are very talented and creative. But you know what else you need to be? Organized. You need to put your pencils back in the box when you are done. Otherwise, you might lose them or make a mess."

Lily nodded and said, "You are right, mom. I'm sorry. I forgot to put them back. I was so excited to show you my picture. I will go and put them back now."

She ran back to her desk and picked up her pencils. She put them back in the box and closed the lid. She felt good and proud. She learned to be organized and to take care of her things. She also learned to love and appreciate her family. She was a happy girl.

Tom felt sorry. He did not know the cable was dangerous. He did not want to get hurt. He hugged Mom and said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I just had a question. What is the cable for?"

Mom smiled and kissed him. She explained, "The cable is for the electricity. The electricity makes the light work. It comes from the wall and goes to the lamp. But you should never touch the cable or the wall. Only grown-ups can do that. Do you understand?"

Tom nodded. He understood. He said, "Thank you, Mom. I won't touch the cable again. Can I have a story?"

Mom agreed. She tucked him in and read him a story. Tom listened and felt sleepy. He closed his eyes and dreamed of happy things. He was not restless anymore. He was calm and cozy.

"Look, Lily, the fan can make my hair fly!" Tom said. He put his head close to the fan and laughed.

"Be careful, Tom, the fan can hurt you!" Lily said. She was scared of the fan. She did not like the cold air.

Tom did not listen to Lily. He wanted to touch the fan. He reached out his hand and tried to grab the fan.

"Ow!" Tom cried. The fan slapped his hand hard. It made a red mark on his skin. It hurt a lot.

Lily ran to Tom and hugged him. She felt sorry for him.

"Let's turn off the fan and play with something else," Lily said. She took Tom's hand and led him to their toy box. They found some blocks and cars and dolls. They forgot about the fan and had fun.

Lila was a girl who liked to play outside. She had a ball, a doll, and a bike. She was glad when the sun was bright and the sky was blue. She liked to run, jump, and sing.

One day, she saw a big black bird on a tree. It had shiny eyes and a sharp beak. It made a loud sound: "Caw, caw, caw!" Lila was curious. She wanted to see the bird up close. She left her ball, her doll, and her bike on the grass and climbed the tree.

The bird was a raven. It did not like Lila. It thought she was a thief who wanted to take its nest. It flapped its wings and pecked at Lila's hair. Lila was scared. She cried: "Stop, stop, stop! I just want to be your friend!"
