She walked up to him and said, "Hi, I am Lily. Do you want to dance with me?" Sam looked up and shook his head. He said, "No, thank you. I do not like to dance. I like to read." Lily felt sad. She liked to read, too, but she liked to dance more. She said, "Please, can you dance with me? Just for a little bit. It is fun. I will be gentle. I will not pull you or push you. I will just hold your hand and spin around." Sam looked at her and saw that she was smiling and kind. He felt curious and brave. He said, "Okay, I will try. But only for a little bit."

Lily was happy. She took his hand and led him to the middle of the room. She showed him how to dance. She moved her feet and swung her arms. She twirled and jumped and clapped. She was gentle and careful. She did not let go of his hand. She said, "See, it is fun. You are doing great. You are a good dancer." Sam felt surprised and happy. He liked to dance. He liked to move and laugh and play. He liked to hold Lily's hand. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good dancer, too. You are a good friend."

They danced and danced until the bell rang. They hugged and smiled. They went back to their seats. They said, "See you tomorrow. Let's dance again." They were happy. They were friends. They loved to dance.

Sara and Tom were best friends. They liked to play together every day. Sometimes they played with dolls, sometimes they played with cars, and sometimes they watched television.

One day, Sara saw a new show on television. It was about adorable animals that had adventures. Sara wanted to watch it, but Tom did not. He wanted to watch a show about robots that fought.

"Can we watch my show, please?" Sara asked.

"No, I want to watch my show. It is more fun," Tom said.

They argued for a long time. They did not share the television. They did not play together. They were not happy.

Then, Sara had an idea. She remembered that her neighbor, Lily, had a television too. Maybe she could borrow it and watch her show there.

"Can I borrow your television, Lily?" Sara asked.

"Sure, you can. But only if you ask nicely and return it later," Lily said.

"Thank you, Lily. You are very kind," Sara said.

Sara took the television to her room and watched her show. She saw the adorable animals and smiled. She liked the show very much.

But then, she heard a knock on the door. It was Tom.

"Sara, I am sorry. I was selfish. Can we watch your show together?" Tom asked.

Sara felt sorry too. She missed her friend. She wanted to share the television with him.

"Of course, Tom. Come in. We can watch my show and then your show. We can take turns," Sara said.

Tom and Sara hugged and watched the television together. They learned about the animals and the robots. They laughed and had fun.

They realized that borrowing and sharing were better than fighting and keeping. They were happy again. They were best friends.

Tim told his dad about the crow. His dad said, "Maybe the crow is hungry too. Maybe it has no friends. Maybe it needs some help." Tim thought about it. He did not like the crow, but he did not want it to be sad.

The next day, Tim went to the park again. He saw the crow sitting on a tree. He took out a piece of bread and threw it to the crow. The crow caught it and ate it. Then it flew down and landed near Tim. It looked at him with its shiny eyes. It made a soft sound.

Tim was surprised. He reached out his hand and the crow let him touch its feathers. They were smooth and warm. The crow made another sound. It sounded like "thank you". Tim smiled. He made a new friend.

Tim's dad was a barber. He cut people's hair and made them look nice. He was very helpful. He gave Tim a haircut every month. He also gave haircuts to the birds in the park. He used scissors and a comb. He trimmed their feathers and made them look neat. The birds liked him. They sang to him and gave him feathers as gifts.

Tim and his dad loved the birds in the park. They fed them and cared for them. They were happy. The crow was happy too. It stayed with Tim and his dad. It learned to say more words. It said "hello", "goodbye", and "I love you". It was a smart and friendly crow. It was part of the family.

Anna loved to play in the garden. She liked to look at the flowers and the bugs and the birds. One day, she saw something shiny under a big leaf. She lifted the leaf and found a fairy!

The fairy was very small and had wings like a butterfly. She wore a dress made of petals and a crown of jewels. She looked at Anna and smiled.

"Hello, little girl," the fairy said. "I am Lily, the fairy of the garden. You are very kind to help me. I was hiding from a mean cat that wanted to catch me."

Anna was happy to meet a fairy. She wanted to be friends with her. She asked, "Can I play with you, Lily? Can you show me your magic?"

Lily nodded. "Of course, Anna. I can show you many wonderful things. But first, you have to promise me something. You have to keep me a secret. You can't tell anyone about me, not even your mom or dad. Do you understand?"

Anna nodded. She promised to keep Lily a secret. She was curious about her magic. She followed Lily to a corner of the garden, where there was a big rock. Lily said, "This is my home. I have a door under the rock. But the rock is very heavy. I need your help to move it. Can you push it with me?"

Anna agreed. She pushed the rock with Lily. But the rock was too heavy for them. They could not move it. Anna felt sad. She wanted to see Lily's home. She wondered what was inside.

Then, she heard a voice behind her. It was her mom. She had come to look for her. She saw Anna and Lily by the rock. She was surprised. She said, "Anna, what are you doing? Who is this?"

Anna turned around. She saw her mom. She was scared. She had broken her promise. She did not know what to say. She looked at Lily. Lily looked at her. They both knew they were in trouble.

Tom and Lily were going to visit their grandma, who lived on the other side of the mountain. They packed their bags and got in the car with their mom and dad. They were very excited to see grandma and eat her spicy cookies.

But on the way, they saw a big line of cars that stopped moving. Their dad said there was a delay because of an accident. He said they had to wait until the road was clear. Tom and Lily were sad and bored. They wanted to get to grandma's house soon.

"Can we play a game?" Lily asked.

"Sure, what game do you want to play?" Tom said.

"I spy with my little eye, something that is green," Lily said.

Tom looked around and saw many green things. He saw trees, grass, leaves, and signs. He guessed them all, but Lily said no.

"What is it then?" Tom said.

"It's the mountain!" Lily said, pointing to the big green hill that they had to cross.

Tom laughed and said, "That's not fair, the mountain is too big and too far. You have to pick something smaller and closer."

"Okay, okay, your turn then," Lily said.

Tom thought for a moment and said, "I spy with my little eye, something that is red."

Lily looked around and saw some red things. She saw cars, lights, flowers, and hats. She guessed them all, but Tom said no.

"What is it then?" Lily said.

"It's your tongue!" Tom said, sticking out his tongue and making a funny face.

Lily laughed and said, "That's not fair, your tongue is too small and too hidden. You have to pick something bigger and more visible."

They kept playing the game, making each other laugh and guess. They forgot about the delay and the time. Soon, the cars started moving again and they crossed the mountain. They arrived at grandma's house and hugged her. She gave them her spicy cookies and they ate them happily. They had a lot of fun with grandma and told her about their game. Grandma said they were very clever and creative. Tom and Lily smiled and thanked her. They loved grandma and her spicy cookies.

One day, a little bird flew away from his nest to look for food. He saw many things in the sky and on the ground, but he did not recognize any of them. He felt lost and scared.

He flew over a big house with many windows and a shiny roof. He thought it might be a good place to find some food. He landed on a window sill and looked inside. He saw a boy and a girl playing with many toys. They had dolls, cars, books, and balls. The bird thought they were very wealthy and happy.

He tapped on the window with his beak, hoping they would notice him and share some food. The boy and the girl heard the noise and turned to see the bird. They smiled and ran to the window. They opened it and said hello to the bird.

"Hello, little bird. What is your name?" the girl asked.

"I don't have a name. I am just a bird," the bird said.

"Where do you live? Do you have a nest?" the boy asked.

"I do have a nest, but I don't know where it is. I flew away and got lost," the bird said.

"That's sad. Do you want to stay with us? We have plenty of food and toys. You can be our friend," the girl said.

The bird thought for a moment. He liked the boy and the girl, and he was hungry and tired. But he also missed his nest and his family. He did not know what to do.

"Thank you, but I have to find my nest. I love my family and they are waiting for me. Maybe I can visit you another day," the bird said.

"Okay, we understand. We hope you find your nest soon. Goodbye, little bird," the boy and the girl said.

They gave the bird some bread crumbs and a drink of water. Then they closed the window and waved goodbye. The bird thanked them and flew away. He felt a little better and more hopeful. He looked around and saw a familiar tree. He recognized it as the one where his nest was. He flew towards it and saw his family. They were happy to see him and welcomed him back. The bird was happy too. He realized that he was wealthy in his own way. He had a nest, a family, and some new friends. He did not need anything else.

Sara and Ben nodded. They understood that the drain was not a good place to play.

"Can we have our cars back, please?" Ben asked.

Mom smiled. She was compassionate. She knew that Sara and Ben were curious and did not mean to be bad. She reached into the tub and took out their cars. She dried them with a towel and gave them back to the children.

"Here you go," she said. "But next time, please play with your cars somewhere else. And don't fight with each other. You are brother and sister. You should be kind and share."

Sara and Ben hugged their mom and said sorry. They also hugged each other and said sorry. They decided to play with their cars in the living room instead. They were happy and peaceful. They did not fight over the drain anymore.

"No, this is my doll. You have your truck," Anna said.

"Please, just for a little bit. I'll give it back soon," Tom said.

"No, no, no. Go away," Anna said. She hugged her doll and turned away from Tom.

Tom was angry. He wanted the doll very much. He looked around and saw a cookie jar on the table. He had an idea. He walked to the table and reached for the jar. He thought Anna would see him and want a cookie too. Then he could trade the cookie for the doll.

But Anna did not see him. She was busy combing her doll's hair. Tom opened the jar and took a cookie. He bit it and smiled. It was sweet and crunchy. He wanted another one. He put his finger in the jar and grabbed another cookie.

But he did not know that Mom was watching him from the kitchen. She saw him take the first cookie and the second one. She was not happy. She walked to the living room and said in a loud voice:

"Tom, what are you doing? You know you are not allowed to have cookies before dinner. Put them back in the jar right now."

Tom was scared. He saw Mom's angry face and heard her loud voice. He wanted to resist. He wanted to keep the cookies. But he knew he was in trouble. He dropped the cookies in the jar and said in a small voice:

"Sorry, Mom. I was hungry."

Mom shook her head and said:

"That's no excuse, Tom. You have to wait for dinner. And you have to share your toys with Anna. She is your sister and you should be nice to her."

Tom felt bad. He knew Mom was right. He looked at Anna and said:

"Sorry, Anna. Can I play with your doll for a while?"

Anna smiled and said:

"Okay, Tom. But only for a while. And you have to be gentle with her."

Tom nodded and took the doll. He gave Anna his truck. They played together and forgot about the cookies. Mom smiled and went back to the kitchen. She was glad they made up. She hoped they would not fight again. She decided to make them some cookies for dessert. She knew they would like that.

Once upon a time, there was a little duckling named Ducky. One day, Ducky went for a swim in the pond. Suddenly, a big wave came and Ducky got scared. Ducky tried to swim back to the shore, but the wave was too strong. Ducky felt helpless and started to cry.

Just then, a friendly beaver named Benny saw what happened. Benny quickly grabbed his brush and ran to the pond. Benny saw Ducky struggling in the water and knew he had to help. Benny jumped into the water and started to splash around to create a smaller wave. The smaller wave helped Ducky swim back to the shore safely.

Ducky was so happy and grateful for Benny's help. Ducky and Benny became good friends and went on many adventures together. From that day on, Ducky knew that if he ever needed help, Benny would be there to splash and brush away any troubles.

Tim and Sam decided to watch the film. They laughed and had fun as they watched it. When the film was over, they both agreed it was a great day. They put the film back in the enormous box and went outside to play.

One day, a little bunny named Bobo was playing in the forest. He loved to spring high into the air and land on the soft grass. As he played, he found a big circle on the ground. It was made of colorful stones. Bobo felt confused. He had never seen a circle like this before.

Bobo saw his friend, a bird named Chirpy, flying near the circle. "Chirpy, what is this circle?" he asked. Chirpy looked at the circle and said, "I don't know, Bobo. Let's find out together!" So they both started to look around the circle, trying to understand what it was.

After some time, they met an old wise turtle named Mr. Slow. "Mr. Slow, can you help us? We found a circle and we are confused," said Bobo. Mr. Slow smiled and said, "That circle is a special place. When friends hold hands and stand in the circle, they can make a wish." Bobo and Chirpy were happy to learn about the magic circle. They held hands, stood in the circle, and made a wish to be friends forever.

Once upon a time, in a small pond, there lived a lonely fish named Fin. Fin was sad because he had no friends to play with. All the other fish in the pond liked to swim fast and play games, but Fin was too slow to keep up with them.

One day, while Fin was swimming slowly, he saw a big fish named Bubbles. Bubbles was trying to strike a small rock with his tail, but he couldn't do it. Fin swam up to Bubbles and asked him why he was trying to strike the rock. Bubbles told Fin that he wanted to break the rock so that he could find a new place to hide.

Fin thought for a moment and then told Bubbles that he could help him. Fin used his strong tail to strike the rock and break it into pieces. Bubbles was very happy and thanked Fin for his help. From that day on, Bubbles and Fin became best friends and swam together all the time.

The other fish in the pond saw how Fin and Bubbles were happy together and they wanted to be friends with them too. Soon, Fin was not lonely anymore and he had many friends to swim and play with. The moral of the story is that even if you are different, you can still be helpful and make friends.

Tim was sad, but he still loved his small pet. "Sam, even though you are tiny, we can still play and have fun," Tim told Sam. And so they did. They played and laughed, and Sam was still the same happy dog, just a little smaller.

"Look, Ben, the leaves are so pretty! Can we pick some?" Lily asks.

"Let's make a face. We can use the round one for the head, the pointy one for the nose, and the small ones for the eyes and mouth," Ben says.

They arrange the leaves on the grass to make a face. They are happy with their picture.

"Maybe. Let's try. Hello, leaf face, can you talk?" Ben says.

Tom and Jen were two mice who lived in a big barn. They liked to play and explore, but they also had to be careful of the cat who guarded the barn. One day, they found a big barrel full of corn. They were very happy and hungry, and decided to eat some of the corn.

"Yum, this is so good!" said Tom, nibbling on a kernel.

"Me too, I love corn!" said Jen, stuffing her cheeks.

They ate and ate, until they felt very full and sleepy. They decided to take a nap inside the barrel, where it was warm and cozy.

"Good night, Tom," said Jen, curling up next to him.

"Good night, Jen," said Tom, closing his eyes.

They fell asleep, and did not hear the cat sneaking into the barn. The cat smelled the corn, and saw the barrel. He was curious and hungry, and decided to check it out. He jumped on top of the barrel, and pushed it with his paw. The barrel started to roll, and made a loud noise.

Tom and Jen woke up, and felt the barrel moving. They were scared and dizzy, and did not know what was happening. They tried to get out, but the barrel was too high and fast. They screamed and cried, and hoped someone would help them.

The barrel rolled out of the barn, and down the hill. It bumped and crashed, and finally stopped at the bottom. Tom and Jen were shaken and bruised, and very lucky to be alive. They crawled out of the barrel, and saw the cat running after them. They ran as fast as they could, and hid under a bush.

The cat was angry and frustrated, and could not find them. He gave up, and went back to the barn. Tom and Jen were relieved, and hugged each other.

"Tom, I'm sorry, this was a bad idea," said Jen, sobbing.

"Jen, I'm sorry too, we should have been more careful," said Tom, comforting her.

They learned their lesson, and never went near the barrel again. They also learned to be grateful for what they had, and not to be greedy. They went back to their home, and thanked their friends for looking after them. They were happy and safe, and never forgot their adventure.

"Hello, bird!" Anna says. "Why do you wear a hat and a coat?"

The bird speaks. "I am a messenger bird. I work for the king. He sends me to do tasks. He is very wise and kind."

"What kind of tasks do you do?" Ben asks.

"I carry letters and gifts to other kings and queens. Sometimes I also bring back news and stories. It is fun and important."

"Wow, that sounds cool!" Anna says. "Can we help you with your tasks?"

The bird thinks. "Well, I have one task left today. I have to deliver this ring to the queen of the flowers. She lives in a garden far away. But it is a long way and I am tired. Maybe you can help me."

"Sure, we can help you!" Ben says. "How can we do that?"

The bird gives them the ring. "You can take this bus to the garden. It is the yellow one with the flowers on it. When you get there, look for the biggest rose. The queen lives inside. Give her the ring and say it is from the king. Then come back and tell me what she says."

Anna and Ben agree. They thank the bird and take the ring. They run to the bus stop and wait for the yellow bus. They are happy and excited. They want to do the task well and make the king and the bird proud. They also want to see the queen of the flowers and her garden. They think it will be very beautiful. They hope she will like the ring.

Tommy loved to play with his toy cars. He had many cars of different colors and sizes. He liked to make them zoom and crash and roar. He pretended they were racing or chasing or escaping.

One day, he found a new car in his toy box. It was big and shiny and red. It had a sticker that said "Mechanic". Tommy wondered what that meant. He picked up the car and pressed a button. The car made a loud noise and opened its hood. Inside, there were many wires and tools and parts.

"Wow!" Tommy said. "This car is cool! It can fix other cars!"

He grabbed another car and put it next to the mechanic car. He pressed the button again. The mechanic car made the same noise and opened its hood. But instead of fixing the other car, it grabbed it with a claw and threw it across the room.

"Hey!" Tommy shouted. "That's not nice! You're supposed to help, not hurt!"

He tried to take the mechanic car away, but it was too strong. It held on to Tommy's hand and bit it with its teeth. Tommy cried out in pain and fear.

"Mommy! Mommy! Help me!" he screamed.

Mommy heard Tommy's scream and ran to his room. She saw the mechanic car attacking Tommy and the other cars scattered on the floor. She quickly grabbed the mechanic car and pulled it off Tommy's hand. She threw it in the trash can and slammed the lid.

"Are you okay, Tommy?" she asked, hugging him.

Tommy nodded, sniffling. He showed Mommy his hand. It had a small cut and some blood.

"I'm sorry, Mommy," he said. "I wanted to play with the new car, but it was mean and scary. It hurt me and my cars."

Mommy kissed his hand and wiped his tears. She smiled and said, "It's okay, Tommy. That car was not a good toy. It was broken and dangerous. You don't need it. You have many other cars that are fun and friendly. Let's play with them instead."

Tommy smiled back and said, "Okay, Mommy. Thank you. I love you."

He picked up his favorite car and gave it a hug. He made it zoom and crash and roar. He forgot about the mechanic car. He was happy again.

Mom looks at Anna and smiles. "Why do you want to cut your hair, Anna?"

"Stop, Sam! You will ruin the trap!" Ben shouted. But Sam did not listen. He threw the car with all his might.

The car hit the box and made a loud bang. The box fell over and the cheese flew out. The rat ran out from under the bed and bit Sam's leg. Sam screamed and cried.

"First, we need to add some butter to the bowl," Tom said. He used the knife to cut some butter and put it in the bowl.

"Then, we need to add some sugar," Lily said. She used the spoon to scoop some sugar and put it in the bowl.

"Next, we need to add some eggs," Tom said. He cracked an egg and poured it in the bowl.

"Be careful, don't spill it," Lily said. She cracked another egg and poured it in the bowl.

They mixed the eggs with the butter and the sugar with the spoon until it was smooth and yellow.

"Last, we need to add some flour," Lily said. She used the cup to measure some flour and put it in the bowl.

"Can I mix it?" Tom asked.

"Sure, you can mix it," Lily said.

They mixed the flour with the other things with the spoon until it was thick and sticky.

They poured the cake mix into a pan and smoothed it with the spoon.

"Now, we need to bake it in the oven," Tom said.

"But we don't know how to use the oven," Lily said.

They looked at the oven and saw some buttons and numbers.

He showed them how to use the buttons and put the pan in the oven.

"Thank you, dad," Tom and Lily said.

Jill and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They saw a big jar of sugar on the shelf. They wanted to taste it.

"Let's get some sugar," Jill said. "It looks yummy."

"But Mom said no," Ben said. "She said sugar is bad for us."

"Mom is not here," Jill said. "She is in the garden. She will not know."

Jill got a chair and climbed on it. She reached for the jar of sugar. But she was not careful. She knocked over the jar and it fell on the floor. The sugar spilled everywhere.

"Oh no!" Jill and Ben said. They heard Mom coming.

They tried to hide under the table. But Mom saw them and the mess.

"What are you doing?" Mom asked. She was angry.

"We wanted some sugar," Jill said. She was scared.

"Sugar is not a toy," Mom said. "It is not good for you. You could get sick. And you made a big mess. You have to clean it up."

Jill and Ben sighed. They knew they were in trouble. They wished they had listened to Mom.

They got a broom and a dustpan. They started to sweep the sugar. But they saw something moving in the sugar. It was a little bug. It was black and shiny. It had six legs and two wings.

"Look!" Ben said. "A bug!"

"Is it a bad bug?" Jill asked. She did not like bugs.

"No, it is a harmless bug," Ben said. He liked bugs. "It is an ant. It likes sugar. It is looking for food."

"Can we keep it?" Jill asked. She thought the ant was cute.

"No, we have to let it go," Ben said. "It has a family. It lives outside. It does not belong here."

They gently picked up the ant. They carried it to the door. They opened the door and put the ant on the ground.

"Bye, ant," Jill and Ben said. "We are sorry we took your sugar."

The ant waved its antennae. It thanked them and ran away.

Jill and Ben smiled. They felt better. They finished cleaning the sugar. They said sorry to Mom. Mom hugged them and forgave them.

They learned their lesson. They never took sugar again.

They hope Bessie will be happy and win the show. They also hope she will come back soon. They miss her already.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play together. They have many toys, but their favorite toy is a big clock. The clock has numbers, hands, and sounds. The clock can tell time.

One day, Anna and Ben want to play with the clock. They go to their room and find the clock on the shelf. They take the clock and put it on the floor. They pretend to be teachers and students. Anna is the teacher and Ben is the student.

"Ben, what time is it?" Anna asks.

Ben looks at the clock. He sees the numbers and the hands. He tries to remember what they mean. He says, "It is... ten o'clock!"

Anna claps her hands. She is enthusiastic. She says, "Very good, Ben! You are smart! Now, can you make the clock sound?"

Ben nods his head. He presses a button on the clock. The clock makes a sound. It says, "Tick tock, tick tock!"

Anna and Ben laugh. They are happy. They like the clock sound. They press the button again and again. They make the clock sound louder and louder.

But they do not hear their mom. She is calling them for lunch. She is in the kitchen. She is hungry. She is not happy. She does not like the clock sound. She thinks it is too noisy.

She goes to their room. She sees Anna and Ben playing with the clock. She says, "Anna, Ben, stop playing with the clock! It is time for lunch! Come to the kitchen!"

Anna and Ben look at their mom. They are surprised. They did not hear her. They say, "Sorry, mom. We did not hear you. We were playing with the clock. We like the clock. It is fun!"

Their mom smiles. She says, "I know you like the clock. It is a good toy. But you have to listen to me. You have to come when I call you. You have to eat your lunch. You have to be healthy and strong. Do you understand?"

Anna and Ben nod their heads. They say, "Yes, mom. We understand. We will listen to you. We will come when you call us. We will eat our lunch. We will be healthy and strong."

Their mom hugs them. She says, "Good. I love you. Now, let's go to the kitchen. I have made your favorite soup. You will like it."

Anna and Ben put the clock back on the shelf. They follow their mom to the kitchen. They are hungry. They are ready to eat. They are still enthusiastic. They say, "Thank you, mom. We love you. We love the soup. We love the clock. We love to play."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the children to listen to their parents, to respect their time, and to balance their play and their food.

Lily's mom said to her, "It's always good to help others when they feel bad. You did a good thing today." Lily smiled and felt happy that she made the boy feel better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to go upstairs and get her favorite book from her bedroom. Lily was scared to go up the stairs alone because they were very steep and she was still little. But her mommy said, "Don't worry, I care about you and I know you can do it!"

Lily took a deep breath and started climbing the stairs. She held onto the railing tightly and took one step at a time. When she got to the top, she felt so proud of herself! But then, she realized she couldn't find her mommy's book. She felt helpless and didn't know what to do.

Just then, Lily's daddy came up the stairs and saw her looking sad. "What's wrong, sweetie?" he asked. Lily told him she couldn't find the book and didn't know what to do. Her daddy smiled and said, "Don't worry, I'll help you look for it." Together, they searched the room and finally found the book under the bed. Lily was so happy and grateful for her daddy's help.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety was always hungry and liked to eat a lot of food. One day, Tweety ate so much that she felt weak and couldn't fly. She felt sad and wondered if she would ever be able to fly again.

As Tweety lay on the ground, she saw a big ball rolling towards her. The ball was too big for her to move, so she wondered what she should do. Suddenly, she had an idea. Tweety used all her strength to push the ball away from her. It was hard work, but she kept pushing until the ball rolled away.

Tweety learned a valuable lesson that day. She realized that eating too much can make you weak and unable to do things. She also learned that even though something may seem too big to handle, with determination and hard work, you can overcome it. From that day on, Tweety ate just the right amount of food and made sure to stay strong and healthy.

Amy looked ahead and saw a big, tall man. She thought to herself, "I want to meet that man!" She ran towards him, but he suddenly moved away. 

The man said, "Stay away! Don't come near me!" 

Amy was scared. She started to run away, but the man followed her. He chased her through the long road until she fell down in a deep hole. 

Amy never came out of the hole. That was the end of her story.

Mandy and her dad decided to go for a walk in the park. As they walked, Mandy noticed a tall pole with a colorful flag on the top. She asked her dad what it was.

Dad said, "That is an important flag, Mandy. It is the flag of our country."

Mandy guessed that she could not reach the flag, even if she tried. Her dad told her she was right and that the flag was not available to touch.

Later, they both noticed a bright yellow flag. Mandy asked what it was. Dad said that it was a safety flag and that it was to help people who were in danger.

Mandy thought the flag was very helpful. She was right - the flag was available to anyone who needed it.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Ella who loved to explore. She was always looking for new and exciting things, and one day she noticed something at the bottom of a well. Ella thought it might be fun to take a look, so she decided to climb down.

When Ella got to the bottom of the well, she saw a funny little frog. She said to it, "Hi little frog, what are you doing down here?". The frog looked up at Ella and said, "I just wanted some time alone, away from all the noise!"

Ella thought this was very funny and she asked the frog if he wanted to play with her. The frog nodded his head and soon they were having lots of fun. They played tag, they played hide and seek and they even built a sandcastle.

At the end of the day, Ella said goodbye to the frog and thanked him for showing her such a good time. She climbed back up the well and thought about how special it was to make a new friend.

Once upon a time there was a pet who liked to twist. One day, his owner took him out for a normal walk. When they got to the park, the pet saw something he wanted to twist. He bent his whole body and tried as hard as he could to twist it. His owner said sternly, "No, don't twist that!" But it was too late. Just then, there was a loud crack and the pet fell over. His owner asked, "Are you okay, pet?" But the pet just lay still. His owner knew something was wrong. He cried, "This isn't normal!" 

The pet was taken to the vet and it was found that he had broken one of his legs. The vet had to put a cast on it so the leg would heal. Sadly, the pet would never be able to twist again. 

The moral of the story is that sometimes our desires can lead to bad endings. We should always listen to the advice of our elders.

Mummy said "No! It's too expensive". Lily was really upset and this made her feel very sad. She wanted to buy the model more than ever! 

But her mummy said something else too. She said "Money cannot buy happiness". This made Lily feel better. She understood that sometimes it is better to be content with what you have, rather than rush for more.

So, the next time Lily looked at the models in the shop window, she still wanted them - but she was happy with what she already had. 

The moral of the story is: Money cannot buy happiness. It is important to be content with what you have, instead of rushing for more.

The little girl was so glad to have made a new friend. She knew this would be a friendship that would never end.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly lady named Grandma Sue. She lived in a small house with her cat, Whiskers. Grandma Sue loved to blow bubbles in her garden.

One sunny day, Grandma Sue went outside with Whiskers and a big jar of bubble mix. She dipped the wand into the mix and blew a big bubble. The bubble floated in the air and Whiskers jumped to catch it. When the bubble popped, Whiskers said, "Meow! That was fun! Let's do it again!"

So, Grandma Sue repeated blowing more bubbles for Whiskers to catch. They laughed and played together all afternoon. The bubbles floated high and low, and Whiskers jumped and pounced. They had a wonderful time in the garden with the bubbles.

As the sun began to set, Grandma Sue and Whiskers went back inside their cozy house. They were tired but happy from their fun day playing with bubbles. They snuggled up together in a warm blanket and fell asleep, dreaming of more sunny days and bubble fun.

Once upon a time, there was a gray bird. The gray bird lived in a tree. The tree was in a big land.

One day, the gray bird met a cat. The cat said, "Hello, gray bird. How do you feel?" The gray bird said, "I feel good. I like to fly in the sky."

The cat said, "I want to fly too. Can you help me?" The gray bird said, "Yes, I can help you." The gray bird tried to help the cat fly. But the cat could not fly.

The cat was sad. The gray bird tried to make the cat feel better. But the cat was still sad. The gray bird flew away. The cat stayed in the land, feeling sad.

One day, a cute little cat named Kitty went for a walk. She saw her friends, a dog and a bird, marching in a line. They were having fun and laughing. Kitty wanted to join them, so she ran to them and asked, "Can I march with you?"

The dog and the bird smiled and said, "Of course, Kitty! Let's all march together!" So, Kitty, the dog, and the bird marched in a line. They marched up and down the street, laughing and having a great time. They marched in a fun fashion, making their own little parade.

As they marched, more friends joined them. A frog hopped in, a squirrel ran to catch up, and a bunny bounced along. Everyone was happy and having so much fun. They all marched together, making a big, cute parade of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He had a big, harmless dog named Max. They loved to play and eat toast together. One day, Tim's mom said, "Remember, don't go too far from home."

Tim and Max went to play outside. They saw a big tree and decided to climb it. Max, being a dog, could not climb, so Tim climbed alone. "Wait for me, Max!" Tim said. Max barked and wagged his tail.

As Tim climbed higher, he saw a bird's nest with three little eggs. He wanted to touch them, but he forgot what his mom said. Suddenly, the branch broke, and Tim fell down. He cried and Max barked. They both wished they had remembered mom's words.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He had a computer that he loved to play with. One day, it started to rain. The rain was deep and made big puddles outside. Tim wanted to play on his computer, but he also wanted to splash in the puddles.

"Mom, can I play outside in the rain?" Tim asked.

"No, Tim, you might get sick," Mom said. "You can play on your computer instead."

Tim was sad because he wanted to play in the rain. He tried to play on his computer, but he couldn't stop thinking about the rain and the puddles. He had an idea. He put on his rain boots and coat and went outside.

Tim splashed in the puddles, having so much fun. But then, he saw his mom coming. She was not happy.

"Tim, I told you not to play in the rain!" Mom said. "Now, you can't play on your computer today."

Tim was sad, but he knew he should have listened to his mom. The next time it rained, he played on his computer and stayed dry.

"Wait for me!" Lily said. She wanted to go too, but she did not have a helmet. She saw one on the grass. It was blue and shiny. It belonged to Tom, who lived next door. He was not playing with it. Lily thought he would not mind if she borrowed it for a little while.

She put on the helmet and got on her bike. She followed Sam to the top of the hill. They looked down. The hill was very high and steep. Lily felt a little scared, but she did not want to show it.

"Ready, set, go!" Sam shouted. He pushed his bike and zoomed down the hill. He was fast and brave. He laughed and waved at Lily.

"Come on, Lily!" he called. "It's fun!"

Sam heard her cry and stopped his bike. He ran back to help her. He saw the helmet on her head. He recognized it. It was Tom's helmet.

"Lily, why did you take Tom's helmet?" he asked. "You should have asked him first. He might be angry with you."

Lily sobbed and said, "I'm sorry, Sam. I just wanted to go down the hill with you. I did not have a helmet. I thought I could borrow it for a little while. I did not mean to hurt it or me."

Sam felt sorry for Lily. He hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm sorry you got hurt. I should have waited for you. We can go back and say sorry to Tom. Maybe he will understand. Lily nodded and said, "Okay, Sam. Thank you for being my friend. You are very nice."

But then he saw a little girl sitting on a bench. She looked sad and lonely. She had no toys, no candy, and no bike. Tommy felt sorry for her. He decided to be generous and share his coin with her.

He walked over to the little girl and smiled. He showed her his coin and said, "This is my magic coin. It can make your wishes come true. Do you want to try?" The little girl looked surprised and happy. She nodded and took the coin from Tommy. She closed her eyes and made a wish. Then she threw the coin in the fountain and watched it splash.

Tommy and the little girl became friends. They played together in the park and had fun. Tommy was glad he gave his coin to her. He hoped she got what she wished for. He also hoped he would see her again. He did not need his coin anymore. He had something better. He had a new friend.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play in the yard. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is fierce. It has sharp teeth and loud bark. Tom and Sam are scared.

They run to the house. They slam the door. They look out the window. The dog is still there. It jumps and scratches the door. Tom and Sam hug each other.

Mom comes home. She sees the dog. She is not scared. She knows the dog. It is her friend's dog. She opens the door. She calls the dog. The dog stops barking. It wags its tail. It licks Mom's hand.

Mom brings the dog inside. She tells Tom and Sam that the dog is nice. It is not fierce. It is just playful. She says the dog's name is Dusty. She points to the dog's fur. It is brown and white. It looks like dust.

Tom and Sam touch the dog. The dog is soft and warm. It likes to be petted. It gives them kisses. Tom and Sam smile. They are not scared anymore. They like the dog. They say hello to Dusty. They play with him. They are happy.

Sara and Ben were two birds who lived in a big tree. They liked to fly and sing and play with their friends. One day, they saw a big basket of bread and cheese on a table in the garden. They were very hungry and wanted to eat some.

"Let's go and get some food," Sara said. "It looks yummy."

"But we have to be careful," Ben said. "There is a cat who lives in the house. He might catch us."

"Don't worry," Sara said. "He is sleeping on the sofa. He won't see us."

Sara and Ben flew down to the table and landed on the basket. They picked up some bread and cheese with their beaks and started to eat. They did not see the cat who woke up and saw them.

The cat was also hungry and wanted to eat the birds. He sneaked up to the table and jumped on the basket. He tried to grab Sara and Ben with his paws.

"Help!" Sara and Ben cried. "The cat is here!"

They dropped their food and flew away as fast as they could. The cat missed them by a feather. He was angry and sad.

Sara and Ben reached their tree and hid in their nest. They were scared and sorry.

"We should not have been greedy," Sara said. "We should have prepared our own food."

"Yes, you are right," Ben said. "We should have listened to our parents. They always tell us to be careful and not to take what is not ours."

They hugged each other and learned their lesson. They decided to never go near the cat or the basket again. They were happy and safe in their tree.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to their room. She is not happy. She says, "Stop fighting! You need to share your toys. And you need to take a nap. You are very tired and cranky. Go to your beds now."

Tom and Lily do not want to nap. They want to play. They say, "No, no, no! We are not tired. We do not want to nap. We want to play with the red car." They run away from Mom. They hide under the table.

Mom is very angry. She says, "That's it! You are being very naughty. You need to quit this behavior. If you do not nap, you will not get any dessert. And you will not play with the red car. I will take it away."

Tom and Lily are scared. They do not want to lose their dessert. They do not want to lose their red car. They come out from under the table. They say, "Sorry, Mom. We will nap. We will share the red car. Please do not take it away."

Mom says, "Too late. You had your chance. You did not listen. You did not quit. You did not nap. You did not share. Now you will face the consequences. No dessert. No red car. Go to your beds and stay there."

Tom and Lily are very sad. They go to their beds. They cry. They do not nap. They do not play. They do not have any fun. They have a bad day.

Ben likes to go to the zoo with his mom and dad. He likes to see the animals and hear the noises they make. His favorite animal is the gorilla. He thinks the gorilla is big and strong and funny.

One day, Ben and his mom and dad go to the zoo early in the morning. They want to see the gorilla before he wakes up. They walk to the gorilla house and look inside. They see the gorilla sleeping on a pile of hay. He is snoring very loud.

Ben wants to say hello to the gorilla. He says, "Mom, dad, can I go inside and talk to the gorilla?" His mom and dad say, "No, Ben, you have to stay outside. The gorilla might get angry if you wake him up. He might hurt you."

But Ben does not listen. He sees a door that is open. He runs to the door and goes inside. He walks to the gorilla and says, "Hi, gorilla, I am Ben. Do you want to play with me?"

The gorilla hears Ben and opens his eyes. He sees Ben and gets very angry. He roars very loud and jumps up. He runs to Ben and tries to catch him. Ben is scared and runs away. He runs to the door and tries to open it. But the door is locked. He cries and says, "Mom, dad, help me!"

His mom and dad hear Ben and see the gorilla. They are scared too. They call for help. They bang on the door and shout, "Ben, Ben, are you okay? Gorilla, gorilla, please don't hurt Ben!"

The zookeeper hears the noise and comes to the gorilla house. He sees what is happening and opens the door. He tells the gorilla to stop and go back to his hay. He tells Ben to come out and be safe. He tells Ben's mom and dad to be careful and not let Ben go inside again.

Ben comes out and hugs his mom and dad. He says, "I am sorry, mom, dad, I was wrong. I should not have gone inside. The gorilla was not nice. He was fast and scary. I will not do it again."

His mom and dad hug him back and say, "We are glad you are okay, Ben. We love you. But you have to listen to us and follow the rules. The gorilla is not a toy. He is a wild animal. He needs his space and his sleep. You have to respect him and leave him alone."

Ben says, "Okay, mom, dad, I understand. I will respect the gorilla and leave him alone. Can we go see the other animals now?"

His mom and dad say, "Yes, Ben, we can go see the other animals now. But first, let's say sorry to the gorilla and the zookeeper."

Ben says, "Okay, mom, dad, I will say sorry." He turns to the gorilla and the zookeeper and says, "Sorry, gorilla, sorry, zookeeper, I did not mean to make you angry. I hope you have a good day."

The gorilla grunts and nods. The zookeeper smiles and says, "It's okay, Ben, I forgive you. But don't do it again. The gorilla is not your friend. He is a wild animal. You have to be careful and stay outside."

Ben says, "Okay, zookeeper, I will be careful and stay outside. Thank you for saving me."

The zookeeper says, "You're welcome, Ben. Now go and enjoy the zoo. But remember, always listen to your mom and dad. They know what is best for you."

Ben says, "Okay, zookeeper, I will listen to my mom and dad. They know what is best for me. Goodbye, gorilla, goodbye, zookeeper."

Ben and his mom and dad wave goodbye to the gorilla and the zookeeper. They walk away and go to see the other animals. Ben learns his lesson and has fun at the zoo. He never goes inside the gorilla house again.

Suddenly, he heard a loud noise coming from behind him. He quickly turned around and saw a child riding a bike. The child was pedalling really fast, so the cat had to jump out of the way. 

The child stopped in front of the puddle and picked up something. It was a sour lemon that had rolled off the tree nearby. The child then threw the lemon into the puddle with a big splash. The lemon started to soak up the water and began to bounce around.

The cat started to purr and chase the lemon. He ran around and around the puddle, watching the lemon bounce and splash. Gradually, the lemon became too heavy and started to sink in the water. The cat stopped and watched it disappear. 

The child then started laughing. The cat thought it was a fun game and he wanted to play it again.

Timmy nodded and watched as the big cars got filled up with fuel. When they got back home, Timmy wanted to decorate his toy cars. He got out his stickers and put them all over the cars. But one of the cars was empty and didn't have any fuel left.

"Dad, this car is empty. It needs more fuel," said Timmy.

"That's right," said his dad. "Let's fill it up so it can go again."

Timmy was happy to have his toy cars full of fuel and decorated with stickers. He played with them all day long. The end.

After a while, they felt cold and went inside Tim's house. Tim's mom gave them hot cocoa to warm up. They sat on the porch, sipped their cocoa, and watched the snow fall. They were happy to be warm and cozy with their friend.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy little dog named Spot. Spot loved to run and play, but sometimes he would trip and fall. One day, Spot was playing in the park when he fell down.

Spot's friend, a kind cat named Fluffy, saw him fall. Fluffy ran over to help. "Are you okay, Spot?" she asked. Spot was sad and said, "I hurt my leg when I fell." Fluffy wanted to comfort her friend, so she said, "Don't worry, I will help you."

Fluffy helped Spot walk back to his home, where it was safe. She stayed with him until he felt better. Spot was happy to have a friend like Fluffy. From that day on, they played together all the time, and Spot learned to be more careful when he ran.

Mom smiled and said, "That's a good job, Tim! But let's not make a mess." Tim nodded and turned off the faucet. Mom and Tim cleaned up the water together. When they were done, Mom gave Tim a big hug. Tim felt so happy that he started to applaud.
